rules.minor_exceptions_text: A minor consists of at least eighteen hours, with at least six hours on the Junior-Senior level. The minor requirement may also be met with a second major or split minor. The split minor requires a minimum of nine hours in each of two departments with at least three hours from the Junior-Senior level in each department. Split minors must be approved by the student's advisor and the appropriate chairs. The requirement for a minor applies to the B.A. and B.S. degrees, except where otherwise noted.
notes: A major consists of at least 24 hours, with at least 12 on the Junior-Senior level.
A minor consists of at least eighteen hours, with at least six hours on the Junior-Senior level; may also be met with a second major or a split minor.

Grade Point Average: a student must have 24 hours with grades of C or higher in the major and must achieve a GPA of 2.000 overall, in all Ouachita work, and in the major, minor, and both parts of the split minor.
Chapel: a student must earn a chapel credit for every full-time semester (minimum 12 semester hours) enrolled at Ouachita, up to a maximum of 7 credits.

Hours Requirement: a minimum of 120 semester hours is required for graduation. A maximum of 4 hours of music ensembles and 2 hours of physical education activities courses may count toward the 120-hour requirement.
Junior-Senior Hours: a minimum of 39 hours of courses from the 3000/4000 level; at least 12 must be in the major and, if applicable, 6 in the minor.

Residence: a baccalaureate degree requires 60 resident hours, including 30 of the last 36; at least 12 in the major and 9 in the minor must be taken through Ouachita; a minimum of 12 junior/senior hours in the major+minor must be taken through Ouachita (at least 6 in the major and at least 3 in the minor).
The number of hours required for graduation is increased by the number of hours taken in Academic Skills (ASKL) courses.

Academic load: the average course load is 16 hours; fewer than 12 or more than 18 hours per semester is outside the normal range and more than 18 requires permission from the dean of the school in which enrolled. A person carrying 12 or more hours is full-time.
Overload exceptions by cumulative GPA: 18.5 hours at 2.800; 19 hours at 3.300; 20 hours at 3.600; 21 hours at 3.900; loads over 21 hours are not allowed.

Class standing: a student becomes a sophomore after earning 29, a junior after earning 59, and a senior after earning 89 semester hours (table: Freshman 0-28.5, Sophomore 29-58.5, Junior 59-88.5, Senior 89+).

A second undergraduate degree requires admission to candidacy by the dean, at least thirty additional hours beyond the first degree, a different major, and all hours in residence (the sixty-hour residence requirement is waived).

Transfer students who have 29 or more hours of credit must submit a degree plan during their first semester in residence; to earn a baccalaureate degree, transfer students must meet the same 60-resident-hour rule (30 of the last 36) and the 12-hour (6 junior-senior) major / 9-hour (3 junior-senior) minor residence minimums.

Grades: A superior, B good, C average, D minimum standard for passing, F failure, I incomplete, W withdrawal, AU audit (no credit), S credit under the Satisfactory-Unsatisfactory policy (no quality credits, no GPA effect).

GPA requirements for graduation are 2.000 cumulative on all course work, 2.000 on all Ouachita course work, 2.000 in the major, and 2.000 in the minor; specific departments may have additional GPA or course grade requirements.
A special course offered on a Satisfactory-Unsatisfactory basis does not contribute to the required 2.0 GPA in the major or minor.

Section and course numbering: the first digit is the academic level (1 freshman ... 4 senior, 5 graduate); the last digit(s) indicate credit hours (a 5 after the decimal point indicates a half-credit course).
Undergraduates may take up to six (6) hours of graduate credit in 5000-level courses with senior standing, a 3.0 GPA, and permission from the dean and graduate program director.
A student may take a maximum of 12 hours of special courses/individual studies, but not more than 8 of these in the major.

International Study Programs: participants must be Sophomores, Juniors, or Seniors with a 2.500 cumulative GPA or higher, in good standing, and submit an application with recommendations from at least two Ouachita faculty members.
A student may take no more than 6 hours by correspondence; correspondence courses are not classified as Ouachita courses for the residence requirement.
extraction_notes: degree_requirements is empty: the catalog does not state B.A.- vs B.S.-specific differences in the Academic Information section (the foreign-language requirement is a Core menu that applies to all degrees; 'Specific requirements for these degrees appear in each individual school's section').

classification uses the graduation-check thresholds stated in the text (sophomore 29, junior 59, senior 89); the class-standing table lists the same cutoffs with fractional upper bounds (0-28.5 / 29-58.5 / 59-88.5 / 89+).
passing_grades: the catalog's grade-symbol list gives A, B, C, D as passing and S as credit under the Satisfactory-Unsatisfactory policy; there is no P or CR symbol.
max_hours_per_semester 18 is the normal-load ceiling; higher loads are permitted with GPA-based overload exceptions and dean permission.
Chapel credit maximum of 7 is stated both in the General Degree Requirements (p036) and in the Academic Requirements for Chapel (p043).
Music-ensemble cap toward the 120-hour total is 4 hours in this catalog (the 2026-27 catalog states 8).

courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: This seminar encourages students to integrate knowledge and skills from their major field of study with the broader liberal-arts experience provided by the Ouachita Core Curriculum. The course provides a basis for life-long learning, meaningful work, and service to humans in a diverse and interconnected world. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CAFS
courses.title: Child and Family Advocacy
courses.description: This course introduces students to a broad variety of human services professions with a focus on child and family advocacy and evidence-based approaches to helping families and individuals that are dealing with adversity and trauma. Fall.

courses.subject: CAFS
courses.title: Trauma and Evidence-Based Treatment
courses.description: This course teaches students about trauma, resilience, and the importance of implementing evidenced-based mental health treatment models. It exposes students to theory, research, and application of a variety of evidence-based therapy models that are used to treat individuals and families dealing with post-traumatic stress symptoms. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: CAFS
courses.title: Human Services and Court Systems
courses.description: This course provides advanced exposure to foundations and influences of social welfare, human services, and court systems. This course focuses on building a strong foundation for developing skills for future work as a human service professional in a variety of helping professions and highlights the importance of self-care. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: CAFS
courses.title: Community & Family Services Internship
courses.description: The internship consists of a supervised experience in the chosen area of family and community services and must be approved in advance by the Community & Family Services program advisor and the Dean of the Pruet School of Christian Studies. This course will be graded on a Satisfactory-Unsatisfactory basis where Satisfactory is defined as a grad of C or higher. This course may be repeated once for credit. Fall, Spring…
prereq_other: Approval in advance by the Community & Family Services program advisor and the Dean of the Pruet School of Christian Studies

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: An introduction to the field of chemistry including nomenclature, stoichiometry, atomic structure, bonding, behavior of gases, and nuclear processes. Lecture three hours, laboratory three hours per week. Fall.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: General Chemistry II
courses.description: A continuation of CHEM 1004 including solids and liquids, chemical equilibria, electrochemistry, thermodynamics, and kinetics. Lecture three hours, laboratory three hours per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 1004. Spring. 1 W.D. and Alice Burch Professor of Chemistry and Pre-Medical Studies. 2 Nell I. Mondy Chair of Chemistry 3 Distinguished University Professor. 4 E. A. Provine Chair of Chemistry 1024. Fundamentals of Chemi…

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Chemistry
courses.description: Introductory course primarily for students in dietetics, speech pathology, nursing, and dental hygiene. Designed to provide students with an understanding of basic chemical principles and their application to relevant problems in the allied health professi ons. The course may not be counted toward a major or minor in Chemistry. Lecture three hours, laboratory two hours per week. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Organic and Biological Chemistry
courses.description: Designed to follow CHEM 1024. This course continues to build connections between chemical principles and the allied health professions, focusing on chemistry within the body, food, and medicine. Topics include basic structure of organic molecules, chemical reactions, and enzyme structure and function. The course may not be counted toward a major or minor in Chemistry. Lecture three hours, laboratory two hours per wee…

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Quantitative Analysis
courses.description: Gravimetric and titrimetric analyses, separation methods, chemical equilibrium, redox theory, statistical treatment of data, and an introduction to spectrophotometry. Lecture two hours, laboratory six hours per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 1014. Fall. 2701-4. Special Topics in Chemistry. A course varied to meet the needs of the department. On Demand.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: A systematic study of the typical compounds of carbon emphasizing the relationship between structure and reactivity. Lecture three hours, laboratory three hours per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 1014. Fall.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Physical Chemistry I
courses.description: Introductory theoretical analysis of molecular structure, chemical bonding, and macroscopic chemical systems using quantum th eory, classical and statistical thermodynamics, and kinetics. Lecture three hours per week. Prerequisites: MATH 2014, (MATH 3202 is highly recommended); PHYS 2024, 2034 or 2054, 2064; CHEM 3104. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: MATH 2014, (MATH 3202 is highly recommended); PHYS 2024, 2034 or 2054, 2064; CHEM 3104

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Physical Chemistry II
courses.description: A continuation of CHEM 3053 emphasizing classical thermodynamics and electrochemistry. Lecture three hours per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 3053. Spring.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Chemistry II
courses.description: A continuation of CHEM 3004 emphasizing reaction mechanisms and synthesis. Lecture three hours, laboratory three hours per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 3004. Spring.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Instrumental Analysis
courses.description: Theory of modern analytical techniques including spectrometric, chromatographic, and electrometric methods. Lecture two hours per week. Prerequisite or corequisite: CHEM 3053. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Nutritional Biochemistry
courses.description: A study of the structure, chemistry and metabolism of amino acids, proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids and vitamin s. This course may not be counted toward a major or minor in Chemistry. Lecture three hours per week. Prerequisites: CHEM 1034, BIO L 2024. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Experimental Techniques of Chemistry I
courses.description: Integrated laboratory experiments from each of the sub -disciplines of chemistry: analytical, biochemistry, inorganic, organic, nuclear, and physical. Use of synthetic techniques, modern instrumentation, chemical literature, and both oral and written presen tation of experimental data will be emphasized. Six hours of laboratory per week. Prerequisites: CHEM 2004, 3053. [CW3] Spring.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biophysical Chemistry
courses.description: Applications of physical chemistry to biological systems and processes. The topics covered include thermodynamics, equilibria , statistical mechanics, kinetics, quantum mechanics, spectroscopic applications, and computational methods related to structur es and functions of biomolecules. Prerequisites: A grade of C or better in each of the following: CHEM 3104, MATH 2014, and either (PHYS 2034 or PHYS 2064). CHEM 4023…
courses.prereq_text: A grade of C or better in each of the following: CHEM 3104, MATH 2014, and either (PHYS 2034 or PHYS 2064)

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biochemistry I
courses.description: An introduction to some of the fundamental concepts of biochemistry. The structures of proteins, lipids and biological membranes are covered, with a particular focus on the 3-dimensional structure of proteins and how structure produces the patterns of chemical reactions by and regulation of enzymes. The course builds up to an examination of the organization of enzymes into regulatory networks that respond to extracel…

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
courses.description: Atomic structure and its relationship to the properties of elements and their compounds, types of bonding, and periodic arrangements. Lecture three hours per week. Prerequisite or corequisite: MATH 3202 is highly recommended); CHEM 3053. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biochemistry II
courses.description: This course continues the introduction to some of the fundamental concepts of biochemistry. The principles of bioenergetics wi ll be covered, followed by an examination of the extraction of energy from glucose, lipids and amino acids. The biosynthesis of carbohydrates, lipids, amino acids and nucleotides will be examined with particular emphasis on the interconnections between the metabolism of these compounds. The c…

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Experimental Techniques of Chemistry II
courses.description: Continuation of integrated laboratory experiments oriented toward modern applications of fundamental chemical principles from each sub- discipline. Six hours of laboratory per week. Prerequisite: CHEM 3272. Fall.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Laboratory Peer Instructor
courses.description: Student peer instructors will assist the instructor in the preparation and instruction of a laboratory course. Peer instructo rs will engage in individual and small group instruction during laboratory, will be prepared to answer questions related to weekly lab exercises, and will assist in the preparation, administration, and grading of lab assignments and exams. prereq_other: Permission of instructor and completion of the required safety training

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Directed Chemistry Research
courses.description: A course in lab or field research in chemistry. A limit of one hour of directed chemistry research credit may be applied to the requirement for a major. The course may not be counted toward a minor in Chemistry. Students wishing to receive credit for resea rch experiences at other institutions must receive pre -approval from the Department Chair. Prerequisite: CHEM 1004, 1014; and consent of instructor. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Medicinal Chemistry
courses.description: The course is designed as an introduction to the field of medicinal chemistry. The topics covered will include folklore and herbal medicine practices, metabolism, physico-chemical and functional group properties of organic compounds, lead compound identification, empirical drug design, modern computational drug design, and select medicinal agents. Prerequisite: CHEM 3104. Spring of odd years.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Senior Capstone Experience
courses.description: Participants will have reading assignments, prepare written reviews, write a reflection paper, make oral presentations, and d efend results on the chemical research project. The course will encourage students to make connections within the discipline, as w ell as to the liberal arts. Additionally, students will participate in an exit exam. One hour per week. Prerequisite: Prior research experience. May not be counted…

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Special Topics in Chemistry
courses.description: A course varied to suit the interests of students. The course may be repeated one time for credit. On Demand.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Special Studies in Chemistry
courses.description: Treats special problems or techniques in chemistry and varied to suit the needs of chemistry students. On Demand.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Elementary Chinese I
courses.description: Courses in the fundamentals of Chinese with emphasis on pronunciation and oral comprehension. Readings on an elementary level are in Chinese. Both semesters should be taken. On Demand.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Elementary Chinese II
courses.description: Courses in the fundamentals of Chinese with emphasis on pronunciation and oral comprehension. Readings on an elementary level are in Chinese. Both semesters should be taken. On Demand.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Intermediate Chinese I
courses.description: Courses designed to further develop skills in all areas of communication. Prerequisite: CHIN 1023 or equivalent. On Demand.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Intermediate Chinese II
courses.description: Courses designed to further develop skills in all areas of communication. Prerequisite: CHIN 1023 or equivalent. On Demand.

courses.subject: CHIN
courses.title: Advanced Chinese I
courses.description: A course designed to further develop skills in all areas of communication in the Chinese language beyond the intermediate level. Prerequisite: CHIN 2043 or equivalent or consent of instructor. On Demand.

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: The Church and Ministry
courses.description: This course explores the nature and purpose of the Lord’s church and the calling, character, qualifications, and responsibilities of those who would serve the church. Fall.

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: The Christian Mission
courses.description: This course explores the biblical basis for Christian missions and equips students to share a faithful and loving gospel witness in contextually appropriate ways in fulfillment of the mandate to make disciples. Spring.

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Christian Missions Study Trip
courses.description: This course consists of a study trip providing international or national missions experience. The focus will be on the study of missions through classroom preparation and practical application on the mission field. Summer of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Foundations of Christian Counseling
courses.description: This course studies principles and techniques of counseling with attention given to ethical integration of faith in the counseling process. Spring.

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Crisis Intervention
courses.description: This course introduces students to the varied ways that tumultuous life events (such as the death of a loved one, violent crime, natural disasters, abuse, and significant relationship losses) most often impact children, adolescents, and adults, and teaches them ways to direct those affected by crisis toward recovery. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Marriage and Family Dynamics
courses.description: This course examines the background and the principles of effective family therapy. Common family problems and how family therapy can be utilized to resolve these problems will be analyzed. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Recreation Ministry
courses.description: This course explores church recreation, Christian camping, and outdoor ministry. The course will examine theological foundations and practical applications for ministry recreation. The course is designed for students preparing to lead ministries that will utilize recreation. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: World Religions
courses.description: This course studies the major living religions other than Christianity. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: CHMM Internship
courses.description: The internship consists of a supervised ministry or missions experience and must be approved in advance by the Chair of the Department of Christian Ministry and Missions and the Dean of the Pruet School of Christian Studies. The course will be graded on a Satisfactory-Unsatisfactory basis where Satisfactory is defined as a grade of C or higher. Fall, Spring, Summer.
prereq_other: approval in advance by the Chair of the Department of Christian Ministry and Missions and the Dean of the Pruet School of Christian Studies

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Studies in Ministry and Missions
courses.description: This course focuses on equipping students to provide various groups and individuals with a faithful and loving gospel witness and engage in the practice of ministry and missions in a variety of contexts. The course will survey a range of topics offered on a rotating basis including but not limited to practices of disciple-making, pastoral ministry, ministry to students, ministry to children, understanding modern reli…

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Child Maltreatment and Domestic Violence
courses.description: This course will examine the problems of child physical abuse, child sexual abuse & exploitation, child neglect, and adult intimate partner violence, along with their contributing factors and definitions. Students will study offender pathology, and work to understand the discovery and disclosure dynamics often associated with each kind of victimization. The course will also address the common relationship dynamics be…

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Teaching to Change Lives
courses.description: This course develops students’ capability to move from responsible exegesis of the biblical text to teaching the text effectively in a variety of settings. Prerequisite: BSTH 2023. Spring.

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Preaching the Bible
courses.description: This course studies the nature, preparation, and delivery of biblical sermons. This course will investigate both traditional and contemporary methods of sermon writing and style. Prerequisite: BSTH 2023. Fall.

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Intercultural Communication
courses.description: This course studies the principles that impact the success (or failure) of the communication process between people from different cultures. Students will learn to “exegete” a cultural audience and create strategies for communicating important messages, biblical or otherwise, to that culture. Prerequisite: Junior or Senior standing or permission of instructor. Also listed as COMM 4313. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: Junior or Senior standing or permission of instructor

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Islam
courses.description: This course examines the beliefs, practices, and diverse communities of Islamic traditions. Topics include contemporary issues and Christian response. Prerequisite: Junior or Senior standing or permission of instructor. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: Junior or Senior standing or permission of instructor

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Supervised Hospital Ministry
courses.description: A supervised practicum designed to help students increase proficiency in interpersonal skills and ministry in a hospital environment. Prerequisites: Junior standing and faculty approval. Also listed as SOCI 3006. Summer I (at Baptist Medical Center in Little Rock).
courses.offered_text: Summer I (at Baptist Medical Center in Little Rock).

courses.subject: CHMM
courses.title: Church Planting Practicum
courses.description: Students in this practicum course will work with an Arkansas Baptist church plant directly under the supervision of a church planter approved for supervision by the Arkansas Baptist State Convention Church Planting Team. Students must apply and interview with appropriate ABSC staff and church planter and be approved in order to be eligible to enroll in the course. Students in this course will gain practical experienc…
prereq_other: application and interview with appropriate ABSC staff and church planter, and approval to enroll

courses.subject: CHST
courses.title: Freshman Seminar
courses.description: This course engages students in the process of building and sustaining a learning community within the Pruet School of Christian Studies and OBU. Fall.

courses.subject: CHST
courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: This seminar leads students to integrate knowledge and skills from their major field of study with the broader liberal-arts experience provided by the Ouachita Core Curriculum. The course prepares students for life-long learning, meaningful work, and service to humans in a diverse and interconnected world after Ouachita. Spring.

courses.subject: CJUS
courses.title: Introduction to Criminal Justice
courses.description: A freshman introductory seminar introducing students to the rudiments of law enforcement, including an overview of the United States criminal justice system and an inquiry into the issues, procedures, and methods pertinent to the proper function of its various elements. Fall.

courses.subject: CJUS
courses.title: Police and Society
courses.description: A survey of the relationship between police and the court and correctional systems, as well as an inquiry into the relationsh ip between police and other key social and organizational institutions. The course will also explore the philosophy of police as a n instrument of social order. Spring.

courses.subject: CJUS
courses.title: Criminal Law
courses.description: The course in criminal law examines the definitions and characteristics of a criminal act, constitutional limits, and punishments. Students will learn the concept of criminal liability through analysis of mens rea and concurrent behavior and defenses in court. The course explores the concept of criminal law through diverse areas including crimes against persons, property, public order, and the State. Spring.

courses.subject: CJUS
courses.title: Juvenile Crime
courses.description: A survey of juvenile delinquency and crime with special emphasis on scale and causation, as well as methods of intervention, prevention, and rehabilitation. Prerequisite: CJUS 3023. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: CJUS
courses.title: Drugs and Alcohol
courses.description: A survey of data related to the use and regulation of mood- and mind-altering substances in the United States. The course will consider patterns of illegal substance use and abuse, problems associated with illegal substance use, and policymaking aimed at both interdiction and limiting social harm created by illegal substance use. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: CJUS
courses.title: Criminology
courses.description: This course explores criminal and deviant behaviors such as alcohol abuse, illicit drug use, mental disorder, crime, law -enforcement, deviance, and prostitution, focusing on social definitions and causal explanations. Prerequisite: SOCI 1003. Fall.

courses.subject: CJUS
courses.title: Forensics
courses.description: A survey of instrumental procedures and methods for the scientific analysis of physical evidence generated by criminal activity. Students will learn basic concepts in forensic investigation and apply them to evidence processing and analysis. Spring.

courses.subject: CJUS
courses.title: Crime and Deviance
courses.description: This course explores criminal and deviant behaviors such as alcohol abuse, illicit drug use, mental disorder, crime, law -enforcement, deviance, and prostitution, focusing on social definitions and causal explanations. Prerequisite: SOCI 1003 or CJUS 3023 Criminology. Also listed as SOCI 3123. Fall.

courses.subject: CJUS
courses.title: Criminal Justice Practicum I
courses.description: Designed to provide students with experiential learning within the field of law enforcement. Through the integration and app lication of the concepts and principles learned in the criminal justice program, students will develop proficiency in basic police tasks and functions. Fall.

courses.subject: CJUS
courses.title: Criminal Justice Practicum II
courses.description: An advanced culmination of the Criminal Justice Practicum credentialing completers as auxiliary officers licensed for part -time employment in uniformed law enforcement. Prerequisite: CJUS 4003. Spring.

courses.subject: CJUS
courses.title: Criminal Justice Internship
courses.description: An internship with an approved law enforcement agency, court, or affiliated entity. Minimum 50-hour work requirement. Cross-listed as SOCI 4023 Sociology Internship. Fall, Summer, Spring.

courses.subject: CMDS
courses.subject_name: Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders

courses.description: An introduction to the field of speech-language pathology designed to provide an overview of career opportunities, career paths, as well as the skills and/or various certification standards necessary to work in various work settings. Fall.

courses.subject: CMDS
courses.subject_name: Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.title: Phonetics
courses.description: A study of the International Phonetic Alphabet and standard regional dialects. An analysis of speech sounds with an emphasis on phonetic transcription, pronunciation, and effective communication. Spring.

courses.subject: CMDS
courses.subject_name: Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.title: Introduction to Communication Disorders
courses.description: The study of the development of speech in the child, etiology and principles of therapy of speech disorders, including the ar eas of articulation, language, voice and fluency. Fall.

courses.subject: CMDS
courses.subject_name: Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.title: Clinical Methods: Observation
courses.description: An overview of professional practices in the field of communication sciences and disorders. Topics may include methods of service delivery, code of ethics, and treatment of a variety of communication disorders. Completion of 25 hours of supervised observation is required. Fall.

courses.subject: CMDS
courses.subject_name: Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.title: Clinical Methods: Practicum I
courses.description: Overview of the clinical process for the remediation of communication disorders. Supervised clinical practicum experience is required. Prerequisites: CMDS 2023, 3001 Clinical Methods: Observation, and completion of 25 hours of supervised observation. [CW3] Spring.

courses.subject: CMDS
courses.subject_name: Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.title: Voice Disorders
courses.description: Study of normal voice function and voice pathologies including evaluation techniques and specific remediation procedures for patients with voice disorders. Prerequisites: BIOL 1014, CHEM 1024, and CMDS 2023, or consent of CMDS Department Chair. Fall of odd- numbered years.

courses.description: Normal anatomy, physiology, and neurology of speech, language, and hearing. courses.subject_name: Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.title: Fluency Disorders
courses.description: Study of the nature and theories of stuttering, diagnosis, and treatment procedures. Prerequisite: CMDS 2023. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject_name: Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.title: Diagnostic Methods
courses.description: Procedural guide for evaluation of speech and language disorders in children and adults, and effective usage of available tes ting materials. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: CMDS
courses.subject_name: Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.title: Introduction to Aural Rehabilitation
courses.description: An introduction to the principles of habilitation/rehabilitation of communication disorders related to hearing impairment. Effects of hearing loss on perceptual, cognitive, communicative, educational, occupational, social, and emotional aspects of life, f or all age ranges, are studied. Junior standing or consent of instructor. Online.

courses.subject: CMDS
courses.subject_name: Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders
courses.title: Fundamentals of Speech and Hearing Science
courses.description: Basic principles of acoustics related to speech and hearing are studied. Areas covered include basic sound, mathematical computation of sound intensity and pressure, and physiological aspects of acoustics. courses.subject: CMDS
courses.subject_name: Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders

courses.description: A study of the etiology, pathology and remediation of language disorders and articulation disorders in children and adults. Prerequisites: CMDS 2023, 3063. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Public Speaking
courses.description: An introduction to preparing, organizing, and delivering a speech to an audience. Fall, Spring.

courses.description: Readings and discussion concerning the practice and effects of communication and media on society with emphasis placed on car eer opportunities within the communications and media professions. Fall, Spring.

courses.description: The fundamentals of digital photography, lighting, composition and use of photographic equipment. Students photograph a varie ty of situations including sports, student life, still life, portraits and more. $35 Fee. Fall, Spring.

courses.title: Visual Storytelling I
courses.description: Visual media production fundamentals and an introduction to storytelling techniques for video, broadcast, and film, emphasizi ng skills development. The course prepares students for advanced training in the media arts. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Media Writing
courses.description: An intensive study of basic newswriting, grammar, spelling, sentence construction and vocabulary building. Prerequisite: CORE 1043 or consent of instructor. COMM 1033 recommended. [CW2] Fall, Spring. 3000.5. Practicum II. Students working on the staff of The Signal, Ouachitonian, photography, video production, sports production, or Office of Communications & Marketing may receive credit for meritorious work. Such cre…

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advanced Public Speaking
courses.description: The course covers advanced topics in public speaking such as handling multiple visual aids within one speech, introducing spe akers (and being introduced), and moderating question & answer periods. Students will also present eulogies, speeches to inspire, and after- dinner speeches. Spring.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Feature Writing
courses.description: Practice in selecting ideas, gathering materials, conducting interviews, and writing stories for publication. Prerequisite: C OMM 2343 or consent of instructor. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: C OMM 2343 or consent of instructor
prereq_other: C OMM 2343 or consent of instructor

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Interpersonal Communication
courses.description: This research-based course examines communication interactions between individuals. The course focuses on how people attempt to achieve their presentational, relational, and instrumental goals by using the tools of perception, listening, language, and nonverbal communication. The course also explores how certain personality variables may impact an individual’s communication. Prerequisite: Sophomore standing or consen…
courses.prereq_text: Sophomore standing or consent of instructor
prereq_other: Sophomore standing or consent of instructor

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Photojournalism
courses.description: Course topics include production of news, features and public relations photographs for publication with emphasis on creativity and visualization, exploration of news values, picture selection, editing and production of photographic layouts. $35 Fee. On Demand.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Principles of Advertising
courses.description: Course includes the history, purpose, and role of advertising in society, the analysis of multimedia campaigns and the applic ation of advertising campaigns in a real-world environment. Fall.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Public Relations Principles and Problems
courses.description: Studies of human relations problems relating to industry, commerce, and social and political organizations with emphasis on m ethods that have proved most effective in building public understanding and good-will. Spring.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Teaching Speech in the K-12 Classroom
courses.description: A study of the methods and techniques of teaching speech communication in the K-12 classroom. On Demand.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Broadcast News Reporting
courses.description: Writing, reporting, and producing news for television and radio with discussion of journalistic freedom and responsibility. Fall of even- numbered years.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Opinion Writing
courses.description: Research and analysis of critical local, state, national and international issues leading to the preparation of editorials and other articles for use in university and off-campus publications. On Demand.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Visual Storytelling II
courses.description: Advanced visual media storytelling techniques and production leadership development, including producing and directing projec ts for strategic communication, live broadcasting, documentary film, and narrative film scenes. Prerequisite: COMM 2053. Spring.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: History of Film, Radio, and Television
courses.description: An overview of the social, cultural, and political impact these media reflected and/or inspired in America as they evolved th rough the past two centuries. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Sports Journalism
courses.description: The study and practice of print and broadcast journalism as it relates to the sports industry. Prerequisite: COMM 2343. Fall of Odd - numbered years.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Media Analytics
courses.description: A survey of the current state of analytics use in the media world. Students will engage with popular data analytics platforms, learn how to analyze both quantitative and qualitative data, and create strategic plans from their findings. Students will earn industry certifications from analytics platforms commonly used by media firms. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Sports Media
courses.description: The study of trends, issues and practices of the sports media industry including visual media, strategic communications, and digital media. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Argumentation and Debate
courses.description: The study and practice of developing and refuting logical arguments. Prerequisite: Sophomore standing or consent of instructor. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: Sophomore standing or consent of instructor
prereq_other: Sophomore standing or consent of instructor

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Christian Communications
courses.description: An overview of the history, trends, and career opportunities in the field of Christian communications with an emphasis on public relations and journalism in the Christian setting. Prerequisite: COMM 2343. Spring.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Social Media
courses.description: An overview of the elements of social media management practices highlighting the components of building a social media campa ign. Spring.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Motion Picture Script Development
courses.description: An introduction to the rules and techniques of screenwriting for film. Also listed as THEA 3643. On Demand.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Great Speeches
courses.description: Students will study some of the greatest speeches in U.S. and world history. All students will research the historical conte xt and biographical information of their chosen speeches/speakers, present the information on the historical context and biographic al background of the speakers, show (or read) the speech, and then apply an established theoretical model to critique the speech . On Demand. 3801-04. Internship.…

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Communication Law
courses.description: A survey of media law, which will include issues related to press freedom, defamation, privacy, copyright, obscenity and rece nt court cases. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advanced Reporting for the Mass Media
courses.description: An emphasis on computer-assisted reporting in writing for print and broadcast media on issues of local, state, national, and international significance as a means of developing skills in interviewing, investigations, research, analysis, and in-depth writing. Prerequisite: COMM 1033, 2343. On Demand.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Organizational Communication
courses.description: A study of how communication functions in organizations of all kinds to allow members to successfully balance the demands of being goal-driven and people-driven. Prerequisite: Junior standing. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Sports Broadcast Performance and Production
courses.description: Advanced sports broadcasting techniques including vocal performance, broadcast preparation, video production, and production graphics. Prerequisites: COMM 1003; COMM 2343. Spring.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advertising/Public Relations Campaigns
courses.description: The development of a complete advertising and marketing program each spring, including research, target market surveys and creative presentations. Because the client changes each year, the course may be repeated once for credit. Prerequisites: Junior stand ing and consent of instructor. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: Junior stand ing and consent of instructor
prereq_other: Junior stand ing and consent of instructor

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Motion Picture Production
courses.description: Narrative filmmaking with digital cinema gear, including a script breakdown, storyboarding, screen acting, directing, cinemat ography, coverage, and editing of a short film The course may be repeated once for credit. Prerequisite: COMM 2053. Recommended: C OMM 3133. Also listed as THEA 4143-4183. (Prerequisites waived for theatre majors and minors). Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Online Media
courses.description: Students will design and create multimedia Web sites. The course introduces students to multimedia skills and how to incorpo rate those skills to Web -based journalism endeavor. Skills include still photography, photo editing, slideshows, podcasting, audio editing, audio slideshows, video shooting, video editing and Web site creation. The goal: to learn the fundamentals of telling stories online using text, graphics,…

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Intercultural Communication
courses.description: A study of the principles that impact the success (or failure) of the communication process between people from different cultures. Students will learn to “exegete” a cultural audience and create strategies for communicating important messages, biblical or otherwise, to that culture. Also listed as CHMM 4313. Prerequisite: Junior standing or consent of instructor. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: Junior standing or consent of instructor
prereq_other: Junior standing or consent of instructor

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Event Planning
courses.description: A survey of the concepts, principles, and literature of various issues of mass and speech communications, the event planning emphasis focuses on conceptual and practical issues related to speech event development and management. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Family Communication
courses.description: This course examines the function of communication in families and explores various types of familial relationships. The course covers concepts, definitions, patterns, problems, and theories related to family communication. The purpose of the exploration is to develop a deeper understanding of the role of communication in the family experience. On Demand.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Conflict in Communication
courses.description: This course explores the principles of managing conflict in interpersonal (or international) relationships developed by the H arvard Negotiation Project. Research findings from the field of Speech Communication, such as the types of conflict, conflict styles, and conflict outcomes, supplement the primary texts. On Demand.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Media Management
courses.description: Introduces students to the management process of new and traditional media; the planning of budgets, content, and distribution; leading a team of diverse personalities and agendas; and regulations impacting the communication sector. Topics during the cours e include: sources of income; publication/production costs; understanding the expense of each department within the organization; mark eting and market-share growt…

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: OBU at Sundance
courses.description: The OBU at Sundance course invites Ouachita students to immerse themselves in one of the world’s premiere independent film festivals, the Sundance Film Festival in Park City, Utah. Through travel and participation in the festival and the accompanying Windr ider Forum as well as class discussions and assignments, students will have the opportunity to deepen their understanding of film and culture. Spring of odd-number…

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Senior Seminar in Communications
courses.description: Students will relate their communications studies to Ouachita’s Core curriculum, the liberal arts tradition, and their careers. The course also will focus on application of knowledge and transition into professional careers and/or graduate studies. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Issues in Communications
courses.description: An in-depth study of the theory, principles, and literature of various issues in mass communications. Topics will vary each year, a nd may include Ethics in Mass Communications, Research Methods in Mass Communications, International Mass Communications, and History of Mass Communications. Because the topics will vary, the course may be repeated once for credit. Prerequisite: Cons ent of instructor. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Special Studies in Mass Communications
courses.description: Special studies in Mass Communications based on needs and interests of individual students. On Demand. Assistant Professor J. Pittman, Chair

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Debate Practicum
courses.description: Participation in one or more competitive collegiate debate tournaments as a debater or as a judge. Prerequisite: COMM 3273 or consent of the instructor. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: COMM 3273 or consent of the instructor
prereq_other: COMM 3273 or consent of the instructor

courses.subject: CORE
courses.title: OBU Connections
courses.description: This course will introduce first-year students to higher education in the context of a liberal arts education. Students will develop skills necessary for academic success, explore Ouachita’s mission as a Christian college in the liberal arts tradition, and work creatively and collaboratively with peers on an intensive and interdisciplinary study of a topic chosen by the instructor. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CORE
courses.title: The Contemporary World
courses.description: Students will examine major issues in the current world, emphasizing the development of understanding to address these issues. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CORE
courses.title: Composition I
courses.description: Students will improve their ability to engage in written academic discourse, appropriating sources with accuracy, elegance, and integrity. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CORE
courses.title: Survey of the Bible
courses.description: Students will survey the redemptive story of the Bible from Genesis to Revelation, emphasizing how that story shapes the Christian’s worldview and affects life decisions. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CORE
courses.title: Interpreting the Bible
courses.description: Students will learn to recognize and develop valid interpretations and applications of the Bible. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CORE
courses.title: Composition II
courses.description: Students will improve their ability to read and write about texts, observing the conventions of formal prose. Prerequisite: CORE 1043. [CW2] Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CORE
courses.title: World Literature
courses.description: Students will read and write about diverse texts from multiple literary traditions with particular attention to their genres and historical-cultural contexts. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CORE
courses.title: History of World Societies
courses.description: A thematic survey of the development of and interaction between world societies, covering a broad period from the earliest Neolithic societies through the modern age. Utilizing a global systems approach, students will develop an appreciation and demonstrate understanding of major political, economic, social, cultural, and ethical elements in world history, as well as the ability to critically analyze and interpret pr…

courses.subject: CORE
courses.title: Scientific Inquiry
courses.description: Students will be introduced to big ideas in natural science, will learn how scientific information is gathered and analyzed, and will use this knowledge to interact with issues of contemporary scientific importance. Three hours lecture; two hours laboratory per week. Prerequisite: Completion of the Analytic and Quantitative Reasoning menu. Fall, Spring.
courses.prereq_text: Completion of the Analytic and Quantitative Reasoning menu.

courses.subject: CORE
courses.title: Scientific Connections
courses.description: In this course students explore how science informs human experience by applying scientific reasoning and principles to variable, interdisciplinary topics. Prerequisite: CORE 2334. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Programming I
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamental concepts of programming using an object -oriented language. Topics include selection, repetition, methods, and problem solving; introduction to arrays, strings, and simple class design. Includes a laboratory component. Prer equisite: An MPI of 80 or higher, or a grade of C or better in MATH 1003 or MATH 1004. Fall.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Programming II
courses.description: Continues the introduction from CSCI 1044. Concentrates on object -oriented development (encapsulation, aggregation, inheritance, polymorphism, interfaces) and elementary data structures (resizable arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues). Also includes introductions to recursion, algorithm analysis, searching, and sorting. Prerequisite: CSCI 1044. Spring.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Solving Problems with Computers
courses.description: Focuses on solving problems that are too tedious to solve by hand (e.g., large data set analysis, modelling, and simulations (e.g., Monte Carlo), brute forcing large search spaces). Includes the use of spreadsheets and programming (e.g., Python, R). Prerequisite: MPI ≥ 65 (College Algebra ready). Spring.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Data Structures
courses.description: Study of ADTs and their common implementations: searchable collections (BSTs and self-balancing trees), priority queues (heaps), maps (hash tables), and graphs (adjacency list/matrix). Emphasis on choosing an implementation based on algorithmic analysis and properties of a particular application. Also includes generics, recursion, and advanced sorting. Prerequisites: CSCI 1053, MATH 2073. Fall.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Internet Development
courses.description: Surveys the many technologies that are used to program Web-based applications. This includes HTML for content markup CSS for content style, client-side processing (e.g., in JavaScript), and server-side processing (e.g., in PHP). In addition, students will write server-side code with simple database interaction. Prerequisite: CSCI 1044. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Human Computer Interaction
courses.description: Evaluation of user interfaces, usability engineering, and prototyping. Design of windows, menus, and commands. Response time and feedback. Color, icons, and sound. Internationalization and localization. User interface architectures and APIs. Prerequi site: CSCI 1044. On Demand.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.description: Introduces the structure, implementation, and theoretical underpinnings of computer networking and the applications that have been enabled by that technology. Prerequisite: CSCI 2103 or (CSCI 1053 and Junior standing). Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Computer Organization
courses.description: Introduces the concept of a computer beginning with the hardware. Topics covered include microprocessor architecture, memory, busses, interrupts, interface adapters, controllers, direct memory access, and serial communication. Includes the usage of as sembly language to reinforce topics. Prerequisite: CSCI 2103 or (CSCI 1053 and Junior standing). Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Video Game Development
courses.description: Introduces 2-dimensional and 3-dimensional game development using a modern engine. Students will consider memory and CPU utilization. Includes an introduction to vector arithmetic. Some projects will be developed by small project teams. Includes a video game narrative review. Prerequisite: CSCI 2103. [CW3] Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Overview of the field, with specific attention to game AI. Includes considerations for building believable non -player characters (NPCs) using state models and behavior trees, path planning, and decision making, learning and rule -based systems. May also inc lude procedural content generation. Prerequisite: CSCI 2103. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Mobile Application Development
courses.description: Introduces development for mobile devices specifically considering the challenges inherent in such devices, such as adaptive interface design, sharing memory, limited CPU, and battery life considerations. Projects may interact with underlying mobile subsys tems (e.g., camera, GPS, accelerometer) as well as other applications (e.g., social media apps). Some projects will be developed by small project teams. Prerequisi…

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: Discusses features and implementations of operating systems including processes, multithreading, mutual exclusion and synchronization, memory management, and file systems. Includes a discussion of the OS’s role in the protection and security of resources and data. Prerequisites: CSCI 2103 or (CSCI 1053 and Junior standing). Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: Study of the methods used in the design, development, implementation, testing and maintenance of software systems. Students will utilize the team approach in the development and management of software projects and will make use of modern tools to achieve these tasks. Prerequisite: CSCI 2103. Fall.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Special Studies in Computer Science
courses.description: Continuation of courses offered on a regular basis or areas of computer science not covered in the regular curriculum. Prerequisite: Consent of instructor. On Demand.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Programming Languages
courses.description: Comparison of the organization and structure of procedural, object-oriented, functional, declarative, and scripting languages. Additional topics will include language translation, abstraction mechanisms, language design, and semantics. Prerequisite: CSCI 2103. Spring of odd- numbered years.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Database Management Systems
courses.description: Introduces the concepts, techniques, and management of databases and Database Management Systems (DBMS). Topics include relational databases, normalization, indexing, and transaction management. Prerequisite: CSCI 2103 or (CSCI 1053 and Junior standing). Spring of even-numbered years 4043. Algorithm Design and Analysis. Introduces formal techniques to support the design and analysis of algorithms, focusing on both th…

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Algorithm Design and Analysis
courses.description: Introduces formal techniques to support the design and analysis of algorithms, focusing on both the underlying mathematical theory and practical considerations of efficiency. Prerequisite: CSCI 2103. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Current Topics
courses.description: Examination of topics, tools, and/or methodologies that have become significant forces in the field and are not covered by other courses in the curriculum. May be taken twice for credit. Prerequisites: Junior standing or consent of instructor. On Demand.

courses.title: Computer Ethics
courses.description: A study of ethical analysis and decision-making for computing professionals who are often required have access to sensitive resources to perform their jobs. Prerequisite: (CSCI 1053 or Internet Technologies) and Junior standing. [CW3] Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.title: Laboratory Peer Instructor
courses.description: Student peer instructors will assist the instructor in the instruction of a laboratory course. Peer instructors will engage i n individual and small group instruction during laboratory, will be prepared to answer questions related to weekly lab exercises, a nd may assist in the preparation, administration, and grading of lab assignments and exams. Student peer instructors may be required to design a laboratory exerci…

courses.description: This capstone is designed to provide a learning experience that will not only allow students to demonstrate proficiency in th e field of computer science, but also will address proficiencies in the liberal arts major domains of knowledge including effective communication, critical thinking, analytical and scientific reasoning, knowledge integration, social responsibility, and information literac y. Students will be e…

courses.subject: CSCI
courses.title: Special Studies in Computer Science
courses.description: Continuation of courses offered on a regular basis or areas of computer science not covered in the regular curriculum. Prereq uisite: Consent of instructor. On Demand.

courses.subject: CYBR
courses.title: Introduction to CyberSecurity
courses.description: Introduces an overview of the security mindset. Includes discussions of access controls; system, software, network, and cloud security; social engineering; and the code of conduct expected of CyberSecurity professionals. Fall.

courses.subject: CYBR
courses.title: Internet Technologies
courses.description: Presents a high-level overview of the the functionality and implementation of common Internet and general networking protocols (e.g., HTTP, SMTP, telnet/SSH, FTP/SFTP, DNS, DHCP, WiFi). Prerequisite: Introduction to CyberSecurity or CSCI 1053 (Programming 2). Spring.

courses.subject: CYBR
courses.title: System Administration and System Security
courses.description: Presents an overview of administrative duties on workstations and servers as well as hardening those systems. Includes OS/software installation and upgrades, user management (groups and permissions), installing/configuring servers (e.g., HTTP, database), the use of virtualization, remote logins and remote administration. To secure systems students must understand password policies and weak password checking; access c…

courses.subject: CYBR
courses.title: Forensics and Legal Issues
courses.description: Focuses on the investigation of incidents to discover and preserve evidence. Includes discussions of legal aspects such as p roper evidence handling, the use of hash functions to maintain legally sound copies of evidence, court procedure. Covers technical aspects such as password cracking, metadata and file system analysis, analysis of malware and obfuscated code, the use of virtualizat ion, network traffic analysis,…

courses.subject: CYBR
courses.title: Building Secure Software
courses.description: Presents a survey of software development techniques to reduce application vulnerability. May include input validation, software testing, misuse/abuse cases and fuzz testing, memory management, encryption, buffer overflows, race conditions, and deadlocks. Unique security aspects of web applications (e.g., client - and server-side input validation, bypassing access controls with URL modification, injection, CSRF, abus…
courses.prereq_text: CSCI 1053 and (Internet Technologies or CSC I 2103 (Data Structures)) and Junior standing

courses.subject: CYBR
courses.title: Network Security
courses.description: Discusses the security of network resources including denial of service, penetration testing, man in the middle attacks, session hijacking, ransomware, TLS/SSL, DMZ, use of security tools (e.g., packet sniffers, nmap), VPNs, OAuth, and cloud computing. Pr erequisite: Internet Technologies and Junior standing. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.description: This course will engage students in research outside of their previous coursework experience. The outcome of this course will be either a project or a paper of sufficient quality to be published or presented at a conference. Prerequisite: Senior standing. On Demand.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Introduction to Nutrition and Dietetics
courses.description: An introduction to the field of dietetics and nutrition. The course will cover the requirements of the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND). Fall.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Foods
courses.description: Use of food science principles in food selection and preparation procedures. Introduction to food science research. Spring.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Sports Nutrition
courses.description: Nutrient needs and food related issues in exercise for wellness and training for competitive athletes. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Nutrition
courses.description: Functions of various nutrients and their interrelationships with emphasis on personal food habits and selection. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Life Cycle Nutrition
courses.description: Prevention and treatment of nutrition problems common to individuals, families, and communities. Prerequisite: DIET 3053 recommended. Fall.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Nutrition Assessment
courses.description: Methods used to assess the nutritional status of individuals and populations. Interpretation of anthropometric, biochemical, clinical and dietary data as a basis for recommending nutritional care. Prerequisite: DIET 3053. Spring.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Community Nutrition
courses.description: The teaching, science, philosophies, and politics of nutrition and the programs and agencies designed to improve the nutritional status of various populations. Fall.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Nutrition Counseling and Education
courses.description: A study of nutrition counseling theory and methods, interviewing techniques, and nutrition education theory and techniques. The course will also focus on the development of nutrition education materials. Prerequisite: DIET 3093 or consent of instructor. Spring.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Human Resource Management
courses.description: Study of the principles of human resource management applied to institutional food service. Fall.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Food Systems Management
courses.description: Study of the principles of organization and management applied to institutional food service. Menu planning; recipe development; food procurement; receiving and storage; food production; quality assurance; management of financial resources; equipment sele ction and layout; computer-assisted management and distribution. Study of the principles of organization and management applied to institutional food service. Prere…

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy I Practicum
courses.description: Supervised clinical practice in medical nutrition therapy. This course must be taken with DIET 4033. Fall 4033. Medical Nutrition Therapy I. An in -depth study of nutrition from the perspective of disease prevention and treatment, including patient interviewing, charting techniques, and medical terminology. Prerequisites: DIET 3093 and 4063. Fall.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy II Practicum
courses.description: Supervised clinical practice in medical nutrition therapy. This course must be taken with DIET 4043. Spring.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy II
courses.description: A continuation of the study of nutrition in the prevention and treatment of disease. Prerequisite: DIET 4033. Spring.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Senior Seminar in Dietetics
courses.description: The capstone course for the Nutrition and Dietetics Program. The course prepares students to integrate dietetic knowledge and skills obtained in all coursework and to apply the information and skills in preparation for a dietetic internship and/or graduate program. The course will encourage students to make connections within the discipline as well as to the liberal arts. Fall.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Experimental Food Science
courses.description: An advanced course consisting of a study of the composition and chemical properties of food. The course also includes a study of food problems and an analysis of current research in food materials and processes. Prerequisite: DIET 2003. Spring.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Advanced Nutrition
courses.description: Food nutrients, their digestion, absorption and metabolism. Methods of determining requirements and interrelationships of nutrients. Prerequisite: DIET 3053. Spring.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Research in Dietetics
courses.description: Individualized and directed research in the area of dietetics and nutrition. Prerequisite: Senior standing in dietetics and nutrition. [CW3] Spring.
courses.prereq_text: Senior standing in dietetics and nutrition
prereq_other: Senior standing in dietetics and nutrition

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Classroom Peer Instructor
courses.description: Student peer instructors will assist the faculty in lecture and lab courses by engaging students in individual and group sessions to explain and review information presented in class and/or lab. A limit of two hours of peer instructor credit may be counted as elective hours for the major. Prerequisites: Permission of instructor. On Demand.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Special Studies in Dietetics
courses.description: This course is offered to provide competent students an opportunity to do directed study or research in the field of dietetics. On Demand.

courses.subject: DIET
courses.title: Research in Sports Nutrition
courses.description: Individualized and directed research in the area of sports nutrition. The course may be repeated once. A limit of two credit hours may be applied to general elective hours. This course may not be counted toward a major or minor in Nutrition and Dietetics. Prerequisite: DIET 2043 and permission of instructor. On Demand.

courses.subject: DLIT
courses.title: Data Fundamentals & Management
courses.description: An introduction to data and how it is used and managed. Special emphasis placed on learning technologies that support and enhance data management. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: DLIT
courses.title: Statistical Analysis
courses.description: A study of the methods of collecting, analyzing, and presenting numerical data for business purposes, probability distributions, averages, dispersion, hypothesis testing, including one-way ANOVA, regression, correlation, time series, index numbers. Prerequisites: MATH 1003 or higher MATH course, DLIT 1013. Fall, Spring.
courses.prereq_text: MATH 1003 or higher MATH course, DLIT 1013

courses.subject: DLIT
courses.title: Data Analytics
courses.description: Advanced statistical topics using software packages to retrieve, clean, analyze, and visualize data. Students will make decisions based on their analyses and will communicate their interpretations effectively in both oral and written formats. Prerequisite: DLIT 2033 or other approved statistics course. Fall, Spring.
courses.prereq_text: DLIT 2033 or other approved statistics course

courses.subject: DLIT
courses.title: Analytics Practicum
courses.description: In-depth experiential learning experience with data analytics. Students will work with a mentor in the field related to the student's major or area of interest to complete a semester-long research project using analytical tools. Prerequisite: DLIT 3013 Data Analytics. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: DLIT
courses.title: Analytics Internship
courses.description: An applied, integrative experience in analytics where students learn and work under a mentor outside of the university setting. Prerequisite: DLIT 3013 Data Analytics. Fall, Spring, Summer.

courses.subject: ECED
courses.title: Foundations of Early Childhood Education
courses.description: A study of the basic understanding of the foundations of early childhood education including child development and learning, family and community relationships, assessment, emergent literacy/science of reading, and becoming a professional. Fall even-numbered years.

courses.subject: ECED
courses.title: Curriculum Principles for Early Childhood Classrooms
courses.description: A study of trends in basic principles and philosophies and their implications for educational practices, procedures, and materials employed in teaching in early childhood settings. Prerequisite: Admission to Teacher Education and ECED 3123 or permission of the Department Chair. Fall odd-numbered years.
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Teacher Education and ECED 3123 or permission of the Department Chair.

courses.subject: ECED
courses.title: Practicum in Early Childhood Education and Classroom Management
courses.description: Directed practical experiences in working with children of diverse backgrounds in individual and group situations. Prerequisites: Admission to Teacher Education Program, ECED 3123, ECED 4033 or permission of the Department Chair. Spring even-numbered years.
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Teacher Education Program, ECED 3123, ECED 4033 or permission of the Department Chair.

courses.subject: ECED
courses.title: Techniques and Assessment for Early Childhood Education
courses.description: A study of developmentally appropriate practices to facilitate the young child’s holistic development and learning. Teacher education candidates will plan, implement, and evaluate teaching strategies and types of assessments for children in preschool programs. Prerequisites: EDFN 2003 and admission to Teacher Education Program. Spring odd-numbered years.
courses.prereq_text: EDFN 2003 and admission to Teacher Education Program.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Survey of Economics
courses.description: The laws of economics, with applications of each, are presented. Both the micro and macro views are covered, with more emphasis placed on microeconomics. The laws of supply and demand, principle of parsimony, and marginal analysis are among the topics covered, with the emphasis on student learning rather than economic reference. On Demand.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
courses.description: Economic resources, capitalism, supply and demand, business organization, the economic function of government, national income and gross domestic product, unemployment, inflation, consumption, saving, investment, the monetary and banking system, central banking, monetary and fiscal policy, stagflation, supply-side economics, and economic growth. On Demand.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Principles of Microeconomics
courses.description: The economics of the firm, price and output determination, the law of supply and demand, elasticity, utility, indifference analysis, cost of production, monopoly, and other forms of imperfect competition, marginal productivity, and income distribution (wages, rent, interest, and profit), antitrust laws, labor practices, international trade and comparative advantage, and the balance of payment and exchange rates. Gene…

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
courses.description: Theory of the behavior of consumers, firms, and markets in resource allocation. Theories of utility, production, cost, price, and equilibrium. Competition and monopoly. Prerequisite: ECON 2023. On Demand.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
courses.description: Theory of the determination of aggregate national income, employment, consumption, investment, and price levels. Monetary and fiscal policy analysis, current macroeconomic issues. Prerequisite: ECON 2023. Fall.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Managerial Economics
courses.description: Tools of microeconomic analysis for managers are presented. Techniques such as elementary optimization, game theory, linear regression, and decision analysis are developed. Students are expected to apply analytical tools to problems facing managers. Prerequisites: ECON 2023 and DLIT 2033. On Demand.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: History of Economic Thought
courses.description: The nature, importance, and development of economic thought. Analysis of ancient, Biblical, and medieval theories of production and distribution followed by study of modern economic theories. Prerequisites: ECON 2023. Spring.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Special Studies in Economics
courses.description: Given on demand and varied to suit the needs of seniors. On Demand.

courses.subject: EDFN
courses.title: Foundations of Education
courses.description: A course designed to give the student a basic understanding of the foundations of the educational function in our society. Emphasis will be placed on the steps necessary for planning a career in education and the responsibilities of a teacher. Classroom observation will be a part of the course. Prerequisite to other courses in education. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: EDFN
courses.title: Instructional Technology
courses.description: A study of use of technology and digital learning courses of faculty development venues in education and the integration of it into K-12 curriculum. Evaluation of and exploration of quality online teaching/presentations will be an outcome of the course as well. Fall, Spring. Winter and/or May term as needed.
courses.offered_text: Fall, Spring. Winter and/or May term as needed.

courses.subject: EDFN
courses.title: Teaching Students from Multilingual and Diverse Backgrounds
courses.description: An introductory course highlighting the important role that culture plays in English language teaching. Teachers apply knowledge of world cultures and how the cultures of different English language learners affect instruction. Also listed as INTL 2043. Offered online in fall only and in-person in spring only. Fall (online), Spring.
courses.offered_text: Offered online in fall only and in-person in spring only. Fall (online), Spring.

courses.subject: EDFN
courses.title: Child and Adolescent Development
courses.description: An examination of the physical, emotional, cognitive, aesthetic, and spiritual development from conception to age 18 with an emphasis on observation, analysis, and application of developmental stages to the education of youth from pre-school through high school. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: EDFN
courses.title: Teaching Exceptional Learners
courses.description: This course is a “Special Education 101 Academy”, which emphasizes the importance of the least restrictive environment for all students while reviewing the law and responsibilities of all stakeholders involved in the student’s learning. Prerequisite: Admission to Teacher Education or permission by the dean. (Cross-listed as SPED 3083 Teaching Exceptional Learners). Spring.
courses.prereq_text: Admission to Teacher Education or permission by the dean

courses.subject: EDFN
courses.title: Learning Theories and Assessment Practices
courses.description: This course emphasizes an application of development and learning theories to effective teaching practices in classrooms. It includes brain-based learning/teaching strategies, student motivation, and a study of assessment tools for the improvement of the teaching-learning process. Pre-requisite: EDFN 2053, Junior/Senior standing and admission to Teacher Education. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: EDFN 2053, Junior/Senior standing and admission to Teacher Education.

courses.subject: EDFN
courses.title: Student Teaching Seminar I
courses.description: This course is designed to enable teacher education candidates to make better decisions as teachers when working with students. Candidates will develop a philosophy of education based on content-specific, state and national standards, and a field experience component. The course will also provide an overview of the basis for school organization and appropriate teaching strategies, including scheduling, curriculum des…

courses.subject: EDFN
courses.title: Student Teaching Seminar II
courses.description: This course focuses on the integration of the university experience, lessons learned, and what it means to be ready to enter the education profession. Reflection on student teaching and required professional development for student teachers is part of this course. Prerequisites: Approval to do student teaching. [CW3] Spring.

courses.subject: EDFN
courses.title: Student Teaching I
courses.description: Provides for observation, participation, and responsible teaching experience in a public school system. Prerequisites: Approval to do student teaching. Fall.

courses.subject: EDFN
courses.title: Student Teaching II
