courses.description: Provides for observation, participation, and responsible teaching experience in a public school. Prerequisites: Approval to do student teaching. Spring.

courses.subject: ELED
courses.title: Reading: Children’s Literature
courses.description: A survey of sources and types of reading materials available for children with an emphasis on reading comprehension and an introduction to the science of reading. Spring.

courses.subject: ELED
courses.title: Art, Drama, Movement, and Music Integrated in the Elementary Classroom
courses.description: The integration of art, drama, movement, and music in the elementary classroom provides both aesthetic enrichment and enhanced acquisition and retention of learning. An integrated approach is in keeping with current brain research which shows students learn holistically. The course will assist K-6 candidates with strategies to teach in an interdisciplinary manner which can motivate and enhance meaning in all subjects…

courses.subject: ELED
courses.title: Teaching of Social Studies
courses.description: Methods and materials for teaching social studies with an emphasis on economics and the integration of multicultural education and inclusion into the social studies curriculum. Pre-requisite: Admission to Teacher Education. Fall.

courses.subject: ELED
courses.title: Reading: Foundations
courses.description: A study of the science or reading including foundational skills, models and theories of reading, and instructional strategies utilized in a systematic and explicit manner for teaching reading. All elements of the science of teaching reading including phonics, phonemic awareness, fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension will be addressed. The field component of this class will provide the opportunity to apply the concep…

courses.subject: ELED
courses.title: Elementary Curriculum
courses.description: A study of content, teaching strategies, and materials to provide exemplary learning environments for children in grades Kindergarten through Grade Six. Discussion of curricula trends and issues as well as state and national standards will be the focus of this course. Prerequisite: Admission to Teacher Education. Spring.

courses.subject: ELED
courses.title: Reading and Writing
courses.description: A study of the integration of reading and writing, with emphasis on vocabulary strategies, process writing, and awareness of the science of reading. The field component of this class will provide the opportunity for students to apply a variety of reading and writing strategies. Prerequisite: Admission to Teacher Education. Spring.

courses.subject: ELED
courses.title: Reading: Diagnostics
courses.description: A study of diagnosing reading readiness and implementing strategies for improving reading instruction based on individual student needs. Use of informal reading inventories, standardized testing, various screenings, and other sources will be presented and implemented to assist with diagnosing reading needs. Pre-requisite: Admission to Teacher Education. Fall.

courses.subject: ELED
courses.title: Special Studies in Education
courses.description: Provides advanced students with an opportunity to pursue independent study on significant education problems. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Film Studies
courses.description: This course introduces students to the basics of film analysis and appreciation. Students will watch and discuss one film per week and write one reflective essay to conclude the course. Open to all students, this course is pass/fail and may be taken multiple times; however, the accumulation of Film Studies hours may not substitute for upper-level (or any other) Spanish or English courses. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Poetry 101
courses.description: Students will study one poem per week with a different member of Ouachita's faculty or staff to increase delight, to gain wisdom, and to begin the process of building and sustaining a learning community within the Department of Language and Literature. Open to all students, this course is pass/fail and may be taken multiple times; however, the accumulation of Poetry 101 hours may not substitute for upper-level (or an…

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Practicum I
courses.description: Students working on departmental publications including Assayers and Scope/Toda su dimensión may receive credit for meritorious work. Such credit will be given in one-half hour credits up to a total of 1 hour credit. The practicum includes such work as soliciting and vetting submissions, designing and editing layouts, organizing publicity, and publishing. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: English Studies
courses.description: This course introduces students to the English major and minor primarily through the study of the genres of literature. A research paper is required. English majors and minors are exempt from CORE 2053 upon successful completion of this course. Prerequisite: CORE 1043, or equivalent. Spring.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Grammar: Theory and Practice
courses.description: This course begins with a review of English grammar before transitioning into an intensive exploration of English syntax, phonology, and semantics. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: The Craft of Creative Writing
courses.description: Students in this course will read, analyze, and write in a variety of creative genres including poetry, fiction, and nonfiction. In addition to producing original creative work, students will cultivate skills and habits central to the writing life, participate in peer workshops, and explore relationships between art and faith. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Literary Criticism
courses.description: Through the study of a limited selection of texts and using a number of critical approaches, this course presents the format and basic elements of critical and analytical writing. Recommended that English majors take this course in their sophomore year. [CW2] Spring.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Teaching Students from Multilingual and Diverse Backgrounds
courses.description: An introductory course highlighting the important role that culture plays in English language teaching. Teachers apply knowledge of world cultures and how the cultures of different English language learners affect instruction. Also listed as EDFN 2043 and INTL 2043. Offered online and in person. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Masterpieces of World Literature
courses.description: This variable topic course presents the chief movements and greatest authors of world literature. The course may be taken twice for credit providing that the topics are different. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Creative Nonfiction
courses.description: Students in this creative writing course will explore the genre of creative nonfiction, reading, analyzing, and writing nonfiction works in a variety of forms including personal essays and memoirs. In addition to producing original creative work, students will cultivate skills and habits central to the writing life, participate in peer workshops, and explore relationships between art and faith. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Technical and Professional Writing
courses.description: Through reading and analysis of selected prose models, this course provides instruction in forms and styles of writing for various technical and/or professional purposes. Prerequisite CORE 1043 or equivalent. [CW2] Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Writing Center Practicum
courses.description: Required course for students in the English Education major, but open to all students with instructor permission, those enrolled in this course will serve as consultants in the Speer Writing Center. Students will attend a one-hour per week training meeting and will serve as consultants in the Writing Center two sessions per week. Other practicum duties may include readings/discussions on consulting, reflective journa…

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Peer Instruction
courses.description: Student peer instructors will be assigned to in-person CORE 1043 Composition I sections, assisting during the scheduled lab sessions to facilitate learning and to coach the Composition I students to become successful, independent writers. Peer instructors will support the instructor in administrative tasks outside of class. A total of two work hours per week is expected. The course, which may be taken twice, is grade…

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Linguistics
courses.description: This course presents a survey of the areas of study which the general field of linguistics comprises. Particular attention is given to current theories, methods, and practices in phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, sociolinguistics, and psycholinguistics. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: American Literature I
courses.description: This course is a survey of literature of a diverse range of authors and perspectives from pre-colonial era to the Civil War. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: American Literature II
courses.description: This course is a survey of literature of a diverse range of authors and perspectives from the Civil War to the present. Spring.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Practicum II
courses.description: Similar to ENGL 1120.5. Taken after achieving junior standing. Credit will be given in one-half hour credits up to a total of 1 hour. Cannot be taken concurrently with ENGL 1120.5. Fall, Spring.
prereq_other: May not be taken concurrently with ENGL 1120.5

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Children's and Young Adult Literature
courses.description: This course examines the history and major works of literature written for children and young adults. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: C.S. Lewis
courses.description: This course examines the works, life, and times of C. S. Lewis. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Creative Writing Topical Seminar
courses.description: Students in this course will read, analyze, and write creatively in relation to a literary genre, theme, or other seminar emphasis selected by the instructor. Sample topics include but are not limited to poetry, fiction, spiritual autobiography, and memoir. In addition to producing original creative work, students will cultivate skills and habits central to the writing life, participate in peer workshops, and explore…

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Editing
courses.description: This course introduces the student to the field of editing, covering five types of editorial work: developmental, acquisitions, content, proofreading, and copyediting. Besides weekly readings and discussions of workplace issues and ethics, highlighted by guest lecturers, the student gains hands-on experience with house style sheets, a copy editor's markings, and proofreading. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: With varied possibilities for writing or editing involved, this internship enables English majors and minors to gain hands-on experience for academic credit and resume-building. The student is responsible for initiating the internship. The internship must be approved by the department chair, dean, and Academic Affairs Office prior to beginning the internship. On demand.
prereq_other: approval by the department chair, dean, and Academic Affairs Office

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: British Literature I
courses.description: In this course students study the chief periods, literary movements, and greatest authors of British literature from its beginnings to the end of the sixteenth century. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: British Literature II
courses.description: In this course students study the chief periods, literary movements, and greatest authors of British literature throughout the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: British Literature III
courses.description: In this course students study the chief periods, literary movements, and greatest authors of British literature from the beginning of the nineteenth century to the present. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Mythology
courses.description: Focusing on but not confined to the great Greco-Roman corpus of myths, this course aims to examine the origins of mythologies and present them as they have been embodied in literary texts. For students with the English, English/Editing, or English-Education majors only, Mythology satisfies the Ouachita CORE requirement for CORE 2233: World Literature. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Special Methods in English
courses.description: This course is designed to provide theory and methodology in teaching English on the secondary level. Emphasis is on appropriate materials and methods of teaching, including lecture/discussion, small group discussion, and mastery learning. Prerequisite: EDFN 2003. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: History of the English Language
courses.description: Beginning with a study of the Indo-European languages, the course presents the various influences of Old English and Middle English upon the development of the English language of today. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in American Poetry
courses.description: This variable topic course presents the chief movements and greatest poets of American literature. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in the American Novel
courses.description: Selections of major American novels are read and analyzed, with special attention being given to the development of the genre. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in British Poetry
courses.description: This variable topic course presents the chief movements and greatest poets of British literature. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in the British Novel
courses.description: Selections of major British novels are read and analyzed with special attention being given to the development of the genre. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Shakespeare
courses.description: This course examines the works, life, and times of William Shakespeare. Also listed as THEA 4223. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Chaucer
courses.description: This course examines the works, life, and times of Geoffrey Chaucer. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Milton
courses.description: This course examines the works, life, and times of John Milton. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Studies in Drama
courses.description: This variable topic course presents the chief movements and greatest plays of literature. Also listed as THEA 4303. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: OBU at Sundance
courses.description: The OBU at Sundance course invites Ouachita students to immerse themselves in one of the world's premiere independent film festivals, the Sundance Film Festival in Park City, Utah. Through travel and participation in the festival and the accompanying Windrider Forum as well as class discussions and assignments, students will have the opportunity to deepen their understanding of film and culture. Spring of odd-numbere…

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Seminar in Values and Vocation
courses.description: Students explore the meanings and limits of work; they will explore and articulate the value of their studies in languages and literature; and they will prepare for professional careers and/or graduate studies. Also listed as SPAN 4601. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Special Studies in English
courses.description: Directed studies in English based on the needs and interest of the student. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGL
courses.title: Senior Literature Seminar
courses.description: Through advanced research techniques, this variable topic course requires students to demonstrate a critical understanding of literature. Scholarly writing and an oral presentation are required. Prerequisite: ENGL 2013 and Senior standing. [CW3] Spring.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Engineering Graphics
courses.description: An introduction to engineering design and the related graphical tools used to communicate design concepts. Drawings will be created by hand and on computer using projections such as orthographic, isometric, and auxiliary. Lecture one hour, lab two hours p er week. Spring.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Introduction to Physics and Engineering
courses.description: An introduction to the fields of Physics and Engineering designed to introduce students to the wide variety of career paths available and the skills necessary to work in a particular field. Discussion on practical topics such as engineering failures and et hics will also be included. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Engineering Lab
courses.description: This course introduces students to engineering laboratory tools and processes by providing hands -on opportunities for using the tools to complete engineering-related projects and test procedures. Laboratory three hours per week. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Statics
courses.description: Equilibrium states are studied by analyzing the forces and torques on both two - and three-dimensional rigid bodies. Topics include structural analysis, internal forces, and friction. Prerequisites: Either PHYS 2054 or both PHYS 2024 and MATH 2014. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: Either PHYS 2054 or both PHYS 2024 and MATH 2014

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Dynamics
courses.description: A study of the kinematics and kinetics of a particle and of rigid bodies in two and three dimensions. Analysis will include force, energy, and momentum methods. Prerequisite: ENGR 2123. Spring.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Special Topics in Engineering
courses.description: A course varied to meet the needs of the department. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Thermodynamics
courses.description: Introduction of fundamental concepts. Units and measures; properties of pure substance, first and second laws of thermodynam ics, work, heat, entropy, analysis of various thermodynamic cycles. Prerequisite: PHYS 2064 or both PHYS 2034 and MATH 2014. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: PHYS 2064 or both PHYS 2034 and MATH 2014

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Electrical Circuits
courses.description: An introduction to the fundamental concepts of electrical circuits, including circuit variables, elements, and simple resisti ve circuits; circuit laws and network theorems; op-amps; inductance; capacitance; natural and step responses of RL, RC, and RLC circuits. Lecture three hours, laboratory three hours per week. Prerequisites: Either PHYS 2064 or both PHYS 2034 and MATH 2014. Fall of odd - numbered years.
courses.prereq_text: Either PHYS 2064 or both PHYS 2034 and MATH 2014

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Mechanics of Materials
courses.description: Stress and strain in structural members subjected to tension, compression, torsion, and bending, and the design of these members. Analysis and basic design of columns and of statically determinate and indeterminate structural members. Simple structural member connections. Prerequisite: ENGR 2123. Spring.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: This course is an introduction to fluid mechanics, emphasizing fundamental concepts, principles, and problem -solving techniques. Topics surveyed include fluid properties, hydrostatics, buoyancy, dimensional analysis, conservation principles, energy, and impulse- momentum equations. A basic introduction to open and closed channel flow will also be discussed. Prerequisites: ENGR 2133, MA TH 3034. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Engineering Materials
courses.description: Basic structure and fundamental mechanical, physical, and electrical properties, as appropriate, in metals, alloys, polymers, ceramics, Portland cement concrete, asphalt, and other engineering materials. Application in the design, construction, and perform ance in engineering parts and structures. General laboratory testing to assess these properties. Prerequisite: ENGR 3203. Spring.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Numerical Methods
courses.description: Numerical solutions of linear and nonlinear algebraic equations, numerical quadrature problems, and ordinary differential equ ations. Use of application software for solving engineering problems. Prerequisite: MATH 3034; Corequisite: MATH 3043. Fall of Even - Numbered Years.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Heat Transfer
courses.description: Theory and application of fundamental heat transfer concepts including conduction, convection, and radiation. Introduction to thermal systems design, analysis of heat transfer in components/systems, computing heat transfer rates and temperatures, and drawi ng conclusions concerning process/system design and performance. Corequisites: MATH 3043, ENGR 3213; Prerequisite: ENGR 3023. Spring.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Transportation
courses.description: This course will introduce students to areas in highway engineering but will include a general introduction to airfield engineering. Highway engineering topics will include highway planning, traffic engineering, geometric design, pavement design and mainte nance, and construction projects and plans. Corequisite: ENGR 3224. Spring of Odd-Numbered Years.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Introduction to Geotechnical Engineering
courses.description: Soil properties, phase diagrams, classification, compaction, hydraulic conductivity, consolidation, and shear strength. Labor atory experiences will be used to explore these properties. Basic bearing capacity analysis. Prerequisite: ENGR 3203. Spring of Even - Numbered Years.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Internship
courses.description: Internships must relate to the emphasis of the student’s coursework (lab or field) and must be approved in advance by the Department Chair and the Dean of Natural Sciences. The course will be graded on a Satisfactory-Unsatisfactory basis where Satisfactory is defined as a grade of C or higher. A limit of three hours of internship credit may be applied to the requirements for a degree. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Fundamentals of Vibrations
courses.description: An introduction to the fundamental concepts of vibrations for mechanical systems, including free, forced, and transient vibration of one and two degrees of freedom systems, with damping. Vibrations of select continuous systems will be discussed. Prerequisi te: PHYS 4003, ENGR 3233. Spring.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Introduction to Manufacturing and Design
courses.description: An introduction to product design and manufacturing, from a mechanical engineering standpoint, that covers the principles, me thods, tools and techniques that are used to create, analyze, optimize and manufacture products. This course will introduce student s to a systematic process to develop a product from the point of customer needs through conceptual design and to developing a functi onal prototype. Elements of e…

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Machine Element Design
courses.description: Fatigue behavior in structural machine elements such as beam supports, rods, and drive shafts. Analysis of stress and deflec tion in and design of these elements. Prerequisite: ENGR 3203. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning
courses.description: Analysis and design of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems installed in residential, commercial, and industrial sites. Prerequisite: ENGR 3303. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Laboratory Peer Instructor
courses.description: Student peer instructors will assist the faculty in laboratory or lecture courses. Peer instructors will engage in individual and small group instruction during laboratory or course review sessions, will be prepared to answer questions related to weekly lab or course exercises, and may assist in the preparation, administration, and grading assignments. Student peer instructors may be required to desig n a laboratory…

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Water Resources
courses.description: Fluid flow in closed conduits. Hydrologic analysis of rainfall and runoff including flood magnitude and frequency forecasting . Open channel flow analysis and design. Storm water management and detention basin analysis and design. Introduction to hydrologic and hydraulic software. Prerequisite: ENGR 3213. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Structural Analysis and Design
courses.description: Classical and matrix methods for analyzing simple and continuous structures. Introduction to structural design concepts. In troduction and discussion of steel and reinforced concrete design and analysis. Prerequisite: ENGR 3203. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Engineering Proficiency
courses.description: The course is designed to help students prepare for the FE exam. Students will review engineering concepts learned during the ir engineering course of study with topics related to the FE exam. Arkansas state rules to become an engineer in training and th e steps to obtain a PE license will be covered. Fall.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Engineering Capstone I
courses.description: Introduction to open-ended design projects that are typical in the profession. Students will integrate and synthesize their engineering course knowledge to successfully complete a project. Students are organized into design groups, projects are assigned, sites are visited, and planning and organizing begins. Case studies in engineering ethics are investigated and discussed. Laboratory two hours per week. Prerequisite…
courses.prereq_text: Senior standing and consent of instructor
prereq_other: Senior standing and consent of instructor

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Engineering Capstone II
courses.description: Projects begun in Engineering Capstone I will be completed. Project planning is completed, design is begun and completed, and the results are presented both in written and oral formats. Lecture one hour, laboratory four hours per week. Prerequisite: ENGR 4601. Spring. 4701-4. Special Topics in Engineering. A course varied to meet the needs of the department. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENGR
courses.title: Individual Study, Group Study, Research
courses.description: This course is offered to provide competent students with an opportunity to do independent study and research or to study special topics in engineering. On Demand.

courses.subject: ENTR
courses.title: Dr. Jack's Practicum
courses.description: Students will manage and report on Dr. Jack's Coffee, Inc., a business run by the Hickingbotham School of Business. They will work as a team to develop a strategic plan for the semester, execute that plan, and provide monthly reports, as well as a final semi-annual report on the plan. May be repeated up to six times. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: ENTR
courses.title: Managing the Family Business
courses.description: This course explores the unique personal, interpersonal issues, and business issues associated with the family-owned and managed firm. Topics include challenges and opportunities for family businesses, the dynamics of family interactions within the family business culture, conflict resolution, estate planning, and succession planning. Spring.

courses.subject: ENTR
courses.title: Entrepreneurial Mindset
courses.description: This course will examine the entrepreneurial process from a theoretical and financial perspective. The course includes identifying opportunities, acquiring the necessary resources to launch the business, valuing and structuring deals, and exiting the business. The central objective is to gain an understanding of how entrepreneurs think, act, and obtain resources to operate. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: ENTR
courses.title: Innovation and Entrepreneurship
courses.description: A course in entrepreneurship designed to explore the development of innovative thinking and venture exploration which would ultimately lead to a new venture. Topics covered include developing an innovative perspective as well as identifying and testing venture concepts. Topics are introduced through the use of creative exercises, team projects, concept identification journals, and discussion of entrepreneurship cases…

courses.subject: ENTR
courses.title: Social Entrepreneurship
courses.description: This course examines the role of institutions in perpetuating or eliminating social problems. The course examines ways in which for-profit and not-for-profit ventures may be utilized to create sustainable solutions to social problems. Focus is placed on organizations that will be partially owned and operated by the members of the communities that benefit from their goods and services. Spring.

courses.subject: ENTR
courses.title: Business Plan Development
courses.description: This course teaches students how to fully develop and flesh out an innovative new business model via a business plan. In addition, all students will present their ideas to experienced entrepreneurs for feedback and have the opportunity to submit their plan to various Business Plan Competitions. Fall.

courses.subject: ENTR
courses.title: Special Studies in Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Given on demand and varied to suit the needs of seniors. On Demand.

courses.subject: FINA
courses.title: Fine Arts: Art
courses.description: Students will examine visual expression and its cultural context from prehistory to the present. Students also will develop t he analytic skills needed to confront art and architecture, fostering the awareness needed to appreciate museums, galleries, and ev eryday life. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: FINA
courses.title: Fine Arts: Music
courses.description: Students will examine musical expression and its cultural context from prehistory to the present and enhance listening skills via a survey of the elements of music, world music cultures, the major musical stylistic periods of Western art music, and American musical genres. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: FINA
courses.title: Fine Arts: Theatre
courses.description: This course explores theatre as a cultural and historic force. Students will develop an understanding of the theatrical exper ience as a unique art form while exploring its connection to other art forms. Students will also gain literary and critical thinkin g skills in relation to play scripts and theatrical performances. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: FINA
courses.title: Fine Arts and Humanities: Europe
courses.description: Intensive study of European art, architecture, history, literature, music, and theatre in conjunction with an extended Europe an Study Tour. Open only to students who have been accepted to the program. Students must enroll during May Term for both INTL 3433 and FINA 3163. This course satisfies the Artistic Engagement Menu in the Ouachita Core. Prerequisite: INTL 3400 EST Preparation.

courses.subject: FINA
courses.title: Fine Arts Engagement Series Review
courses.description: Credit for this one-hour course is granted upon completion of a) the attendance requirements for the Arts Engagement Series and b) an online survey prompting reflection on the events attended. Graded on a Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory basis. There is no regular class meeting for this course. Overload charges are waived for this course. Pre-requisite: Senior standing.

courses.subject: FINA
courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: This course provides a conceptual springboard for using experience to inform life-long learning of and service to humans and the world humans inhabit. Students will explore ideas associated with aesthetics, art criticism, and the culture of artists as it relates to their discipline and will reflect on their four-year Christian liberal arts experience. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Personal Finance
courses.description: Students will survey the management of personal and family finances, including budgeting, consumer buying, personal credit, savings and investment, home ownership, insurance, and retirement. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Financial Institutions
courses.description: Role and operations of financial markets and institutions in the economy. Supply of and demand for funds, interest rate determination, monetary and fiscal policy, flow of funds analysis. Financial policies and operations of commercial banks and other financial institutions. Prerequisites: ECON 2023; ACCT 2013, 2023. Spring.

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Corporate Financial Management
courses.description: The nature of financial management, including financial statement analysis, valuation, risk and return, capital budgeting, cost of capital, capital structure, leverage, dividend policy, working capital management, and international considerations. Prerequisites: ACCT 2013, 2023; ECON 2023. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Insurance Principles
courses.description: Principles of risk management emphasizing insurance; insurance policies, regulations, and profession; the types of insurance including property, liability, health and life. Prerequisite: Junior standing or consent of the instructor. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: Junior standing or consent of the instructor
prereq_other: Junior standing or consent of the instructor

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Retirement and Employee Benefits
courses.description: An overview of the retirement planning process, with an emphasis on retirement needs analysis, types of qualified and nonqualified plans, and distribution rules and taxation. Also includes an examination of common employee benefits and social insurance programs. On Demand.

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Estate Planning
courses.description: An overview of the estate planning process, including taxation and the probate process, with a focus on strategies for the transfer of assets through proper titling, estate planning documents such as wills and trusts, and other techniques. On Demand.

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Financial Statement Analysis
courses.description: A closer look at the review, analysis, and interpretation of key financial statements. Topics include financial reporting, earnings quality, profitability, and ratio analysis. The end goal is an enhanced understanding of the accounting framework for improved risk assessment, forecasting, and valuation. Fall.

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Real Estate Principles
courses.description: Introduction to the field and profession of real estate; consideration of physical, economic, legal, and technical factors; real estate transactions, financing, and management. Prerequisite: Junior standing or consent of the instructor. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: Junior standing or consent of the instructor
prereq_other: Junior standing or consent of the instructor

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Investments
courses.description: Investments principles and practices from the viewpoint of the individual investor with an emphasis on investment criteria, sources of information, types of financial investments and the mechanics of purchase and sale. Prerequisite: Junior standing. Fall.

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Advanced Financial Planning
courses.description: Examines the financial planning process, from client engagement and data acquisition to plan development and implementation; identifies strategic considerations in the application of insurance, investment, education, retirement, and estate planning techniques; explores current regulatory and ethical issues related to careers in financial planning, especially those in the client-advisor relationship; emphasis on the f…

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Introduction to Portfolio Management
courses.description: The study of investing strategies and techniques. Combines passive and active management, with an emphasis on fundamental analysis. By invitation only. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Portfolio Management Practicum / Ary Fund
courses.description: The application of investing strategies and techniques to the Eddie and Phyllis Ary Student Investment Fund, a stock portfolio managed by a team of student analysts. Prerequisite: FINN 4070. By invitation only. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: FINN
courses.title: Special Studies in Finance
courses.description: Given on demand and varied to meet the needs of seniors. On Demand.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Elementary French I
courses.description: The fundamentals of French with emphasis on pronunciation, oral comprehension, grammar, and composition. Both semesters should be taken. On Demand.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Elementary French II
courses.description: The fundamentals of French with emphasis on pronunciation, oral comprehension, grammar, and composition. Both semesters should be taken. On Demand.

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Intermediate French I
courses.description: A review of basic grammar and a study of in-depth grammar with practice in reading, writing, listening and speaking. Prerequisite: FREN 1023 or equivalent or consent of instructor. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: FREN 1023 or equivalent or consent of instructor

courses.subject: FREN
courses.title: Intermediate French II
courses.description: A review of basic grammar and a study of in-depth grammar with practice in reading, writing, listening and speaking. Prerequisite: FREN 1023 or equivalent or consent of instructor. On Demand.
courses.prereq_text: FREN 1023 or equivalent or consent of instructor

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Introduction to Human Geography
courses.description: A study of the earth’s surface and the relationship of its features to man’s political and cultural development. On Demand.

courses.subject: GEOG
courses.title: Natural Resources: Environment and Survival
courses.description: A study of the principles and methods of conserving natural resources, with special consideration of such problems in the sta te of Arkansas. On Demand.

courses.subject: GERM
courses.title: Elementary German I
courses.description: The fundamentals of German with equal emphasis on the writing, speaking, and reading of the language. 1013 in Fall, 1023 in Spring.

courses.subject: GERM
courses.title: Elementary German II
courses.description: The fundamentals of German with equal emphasis on the writing, speaking, and reading of the language. 1013 in Fall, 1023 in Spring.

courses.subject: GERM
courses.title: Intermediate German I
courses.description: Reading of selected passages of German literature. On Demand.

courses.subject: GERM
courses.title: Intermediate German II
courses.description: Reading of selected passages of German literature. On Demand.

courses.subject: GREK
courses.title: Elementary Greek I and II
courses.description: An introduction to New Testament Greek. The course focuses on the forms, grammar, vocabulary, and syntax of Koine Greek for the purpose of translating and interpreting the Greek New Testament. GREK 2203 in Fall, GREK 2213 in Spring.
courses.offered_text: GREK 2203 in Fall, GREK 2213 in Spring.

courses.subject: GREK
courses.title: Elementary Greek II
courses.description: An introduction to New Testament Greek. The course focuses on the forms, grammar, vocabulary, and syntax of Koine Greek for the purpose of translating and interpreting the Greek New Testament. GREK 2203 in Fall, GREK 2213 in Spring.
courses.offered_text: GREK 2203 in Fall, GREK 2213 in Spring.

courses.subject: GREK
courses.title: New Testament Greek Reading: Narrative
courses.description: A reading course focusing on the translation of passages from narrative sections of the Greek New Testament. Prerequisites: GREK 2213. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: GREK
courses.title: New Testament Greek Reading: Epistles
courses.description: A reading course focusing on the translation of passages from epistolary sections of the Greek New Testament. Prerequisites: GREK 2213. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: GREK
courses.title: New Testament Greek Exegesis: Narrative
courses.description: A course on Greek grammar and syntax focusing on the application of a comprehensive exegetical method to passages from narrative sections of the Greek New Testament. Prerequisites: GREK 3303 or permission of instructor. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: GREK
courses.title: New Testament Greek Exegesis: Epistles
courses.description: A course on Greek grammar and syntax focusing on the application of a comprehensive exegetical method to passages from epistolary sections of the Greek New Testament. Prerequisites: GREK 3313 or permission of instructor. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: HEBR
courses.title: Elementary Hebrew I and II
courses.description: An introduction to biblical Hebrew. This course focuses on the grammar, syntax, and vocabulary of the Hebrew Bible with emphasis on translating from Hebrew to English. HEBR 2103 in Fall, HEBR 2113 in Spring.
courses.offered_text: HEBR 2103 in Fall, HEBR 2113 in Spring.

courses.subject: HEBR
courses.title: Elementary Hebrew II
courses.description: An introduction to biblical Hebrew. This course focuses on the grammar, syntax, and vocabulary of the Hebrew Bible with emphasis on translating from Hebrew to English. HEBR 2103 in Fall, HEBR 2113 in Spring.
courses.offered_text: HEBR 2103 in Fall, HEBR 2113 in Spring.

courses.subject: HEBR
courses.title: Hebrew Reading I
courses.description: An intermediate-level reading course emphasizing the translation of Hebrew narrative. The class will translate Ruth and other selected narrative texts. The course also includes an introduction to textual criticism. Prerequisite: HEBR 2113. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: HEBR
courses.title: Hebrew Reading II
courses.description: A continuation of HEBR 3103. Both narrative and poetic texts will be studied. Prerequisite: HEBR 3103. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: HEBR
courses.title: Hebrew Exegesis I
courses.description: An intermediate-level Hebrew exegesis course focusing on the development of the student’s exegetical skills with narrative texts in the Old Testament. Prerequisite: HEBR 2113. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: HEBR
courses.title: Hebrew Exegesis II
courses.description: An advanced-level Hebrew exegesis course focusing on the development of the student’s exegetical skills with prophetic and poetic texts in the Old Testament. Prerequisite: HEBR 4103. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: United States History to 1877
courses.description: Survey of the interplay of forces that have brought the evolutionary development of American economic, cultural, and political institutions from 1492 to 1877. Fall.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: United States History Since 1877
courses.description: Survey of the interplay of forces that have brought the evolutionary development of American economic, cultural and political institutions from 1877 to the present. Spring.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introduction to Historical Studies
courses.description: This course will integrate historiography, a discussion of theory, writing and presentation techniques, as well as a discussion of different career options in order to present a complete picture of what it means to be a professional historian to our majors. This course will fulfill the College Writing 2 requirement. Prerequisite: CORE 1043. [CW2] Spring.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Latin American History in México
courses.description: Accompanying a study abroad course in Mexico, this course will cover thematic topics in Latin American History and contempora ry politics. It will place an emphasis on Mexico and the Caribbean region. This course meets the requirement for CORE 2243. The course will incur an additional course fee. Co -requisite: one from among SPAN 1413, SPAN 1423, SPAN 2433, SPAN 2443, or SPAN 4403. On Demand.
courses.coreq_text: one from among SPAN 1413, SPAN 1423, SPAN 2433, SPAN 2443, or SPAN 4403

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Memories of Contemporary History in Europe
courses.description: Following a study of how people and societies remember events such as conflict and peace, students will spend ten days in Eur ope visiting memorial sites and museums to better understand the impact that these have on studies and interpretations of world h istories. The course meets the requirement for CORE 2243. The course will incur an additional course fee. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Colonial Africa
courses.description: Study of African social, cultural, and political history during colonial rule. Readings and course discussion will investigat e the factors leading to widespread colonialism, differences in colonial life under different powers, and legacies of the institution. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Decolonization
courses.description: Study of decolonization during the twentieth century. Readings and course discussions will focus on the rise of nationalism, construction of a Third World identity, relationships to former colonial powers, and nation-building in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Atrocity and Aftermath
courses.description: This course provides a twentieth - and twenty -first century overview of International Criminal Court offenses such as Crimes of Aggression, Crimes Against Humanity, Genocide, and War Crimes. Students will learn about the history of international coopera tive efforts to define, monitor, and prosecute these, examine case studies, and read about how various groups have advocated for consideration of their respective ex…

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Contemporary Southern Africa
courses.description: This course introduces students to southern African culture and politics during the twentieth century. We will pay particular attention to themes of colonialism and apartheid, politics of independence, inter -country relations, and social and cultural histo ries from the late nineteenth century to the present. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Caribbean
courses.description: Survey of islands within and mainland bordering Caribbean Sea, beginning with the Colombian Era. Students will learn about intellectual histories of the region. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Model U
courses.description: N. Seminar. Students study the issues and procedures of the United Nations. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor is required. Also listed as INTL 3080 and PSCI 3080. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: permission of the instructor is required
prereq_other: permission of the instructor is required

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Model U
courses.description: N. with Practicum. Students prepare for a regional simulation of the United Nations by learning about their country’s history, government, and foreign policy. Students enroll for this only if this is their first time attending a Model U. N. simulation as a Ouachita student. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3080. Also listed as INTL 3083 and PSCI 3083. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: permission of the instructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3080
prereq_other: permission of the instructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3080

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Model U
courses.description: N. Practicum. Students prepare for a regional simulation of the United Nations by learning about their country’s history, government, and foreign policy. This course cannot be in the same department that HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083 was taken. Prerequisite: permission of the ins tructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083. Also listed as INTL 3091 and PSCI 3091. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: permission of the ins tructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083
prereq_other: permission of the ins tructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Medieval Europe, 410-1450
courses.description: This course will cover the history of Europe and its interactions with the world from the fall of the Western Roman Empire th rough the decline of the feudal states. Topics covered will include (but are not limited to): Barbarian invasions, the rise of Byzantium as successor to Rome, feudalism, monasticism, religious conflicts between Popes and Kings, war and its social consequences, and the crises of the 14th centur…

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Early Modern Europe, 1450-1789
courses.description: This course will focus chiefly on the socio-political, economic, intellectual, and cultural developments within Europe from the end of the Middle Ages up to eve of the French Revolution. Topics covered will include (but are not limited to) Mercantilism, Absolutism , Renaissance, Reformation, and the Enlightenment. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Revolutionary Europe, 1789-1914
courses.description: This course will provide an overview of the major political, economic, social, and cultural developments during the so -called “long nineteenth century,” from the French Revolution to the eve of World War I. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The World at War, 1914-1945
courses.description: This course will focus on the period of the two Great World Wars of the 20th century. Topics covered will include (but are not limited to) proximate and immediate causes of global war; nationalism and scientific progress as justifications for violence; pol itical, military, economic, social and cultural consequences of each conflict; the interwar period; and the failures and the successes of attem pts at peace. Fall…

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Europe Since 1945
courses.description: This course will cover major historical developments within Europe and in a global context from 1945 to the present. Topics covered will include (but are not limited to) the occupation of Germany after 1945, the bi -polarization of the Cold War world, socia l and cultural movements, immigration, decolonization, the end of the Cold War and its consequences and European Integration. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Germany and Central Europe
courses.description: This course will investigate major developments in the histories of the German territories and Central Europe from the end of the Thirty Years’ War to the present day. Topics covered may include the German Enlightenment, Romanticism, the Napoleonic Wars, Nationalism and Mass Industrial Society, Imperialism, the road to Global War, the First World War, the rise of political extremism during the interwar period, the Se…

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Russia and Eastern Europe
courses.description: This course will cover essential themes in Russian and Eastern European history through the Medieval, Mongol and Imperial Per iods, as well as from the Bolshevik Revolution through the collapse of Soviet Communism. Topics covered may include the establishm ent of the Kievan Rus’, the role of religious institutions and practices, the nature of autocratic authority, the pattern and process of imperial expansion, Bolshe…

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Colonial North America and the Revolution
courses.description: The political, economic, social, and military history of North America from the founding of Jamestown to the end of the Ameri can Revolution. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Fragile American Republic
courses.description: The political, economic, social, and military history of the United States from the end of the American Revolution to the start of the Civil War, with emphasis on sectional differences. Fall of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Civil War and Reconstruction
courses.description: The political, economic, social, and military history of the United States during the Civil War and Reconstruction, with emph asis on battles, leaders, and the struggle for black equality. Fall of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Gilded Age and Progressive Era
courses.description: An in-depth treatment of the political, economic, and cultural history of the United States in the years between 1870 and 1920. Emphases include the emergence of corporate industry and popular reactions, the rise of racial segregation and early civil rights activism, and the expansion of the American sphere of influence in the international community. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Twentieth Century America
courses.description: A survey of the political, economic, and social history of the United States during the Twentieth Century. Potential emphases include the Progressive Era, the Great Depression and New Deal, American participation in World War II, the Cold War, Civil Rights, the Vietnam War, and post-Cold War America. Spring of even-numbered years.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Modern America
courses.description: An in-depth treatment of the political, economic, and cultural history of the United States from 1980 to the present. Emphases incl ude presidential politics and policy from Reagan to Biden; the growth of the Internet economy and the Great Recession; foreig n policy responses to September 11, 2001; and cultural forces in play after 1980. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Arkansas History
courses.description: The political, economic, social, and cultural development of Arkansas from the coming of the Indian to the present, with special emphasis on Arkansas as a national and regional component. Fall.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of American Women
courses.description: A survey of the contributions made by women of diverse economic and cultural backgrounds to the politics, culture, and economy of the United States from the Colonial Era to the present, with special emphasis upon the role of gender in defining the limits u pon and opportunities for women in American society. Spring of odd-numbered years.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: U.S
courses.description: Military History. This course examines selected themes in U.S. military history from the Revolutionary War to the present. While the subject matter may vary, the central focus will be on war and society. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Museum Studies
courses.description: Students will learn basics of museum management, including acquisition and cataloging of artifacts; personnel and public rela tions management; and working on historical interpretation within communities. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Local and Community History
courses.description: Learn to work with communities, including historical associations, museums, libraries, governments, and schools. Engage resea rch sources for local history; analyze, prepare, and display these resources; and disseminate them to larger audiences. Central t o this course is incorporating technology into content delivery. On Demand.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: American Diplomacy
courses.description: A study of foreign policy in the United States in fact and theory, analyzing America’s involvement in World Affairs from 1776 to the present. Current diplomatic policy of the United States is examined in relation to the past. Also listed as PSCI 4053. Fall of odd - numbered years.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Application of the methods and materials of professional research and writing. Students, through directed research in special topics, will further their understanding of the nature, use, and criticism of documents, bibliographic and manuscript preparation, and the utilization of digital resources. Students will complete career preparation activities and a final, professional-grade project. Approval of the instructor.…

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Topical Seminar
courses.description: Special topics which will vary from semester to semester. Because a different topic will be offered each semester, the course may be repeated once for credit. Students will read a variety of primary and/or secondary sources. Prerequisite: approval of the instructor. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Special Studies in History
courses.description: Independent studies or courses in advanced topics of History. On Demand.

courses.subject: HNRS
courses.title: Honors Directed Studies
courses.description: A special topics course designed to meet the needs of the individual Honors student. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: HNRS
courses.title: Honors Seminar
courses.description: An interdisciplinary seminar designed for the Honors student. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: HNRS
courses.title: Honors Thesis
courses.description: A critical study and analysis course designed for the individual Junior or Senior Honors student. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: HUM
courses.title: Servant Leadership
courses.description: A study of the art and practice of servant leadership, both in comparison with other traditional forms of leadership and with special consideration of how servant leadership exemplifies the life of Christ. On Demand. William Fenna and Emily Rogers Department of Communications

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: Teaching Students from Multilingual and Diverse Backgrounds
courses.description: An introductory course highlighting the important role that culture plays in English language teaching. Teachers apply knowledge of world cultures and how the cultures of different English language learners affect instruction. Also listed as EDFN 2043. Online Fall 1 term.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: Summer Study
courses.description: Appropriate credit is awarded through the following summer study programs: European Study Tour, Salzburg Study Program, Japan Study Program, Lithuania Study Program, Liverpool Hope Study Program and Alicante Study Program. Summer.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: Second Language Acquisition
courses.description: A study of linguistic foundations and functional skills for assisting non-English speakers toward English competency; of particular interest to students who anticipate working in international settings and students seeking licensure for teaching. Online Fall 2 term.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: Methods of Teaching English as a Second Language
courses.description: This course examines current and previous methods of language teaching so that teachers will be able to incorporate activities, tasks, and strategies to develop meaningful and authentic use of language in the classroom. Available technology will also be employed to integrate listening, speaking, reading, and writing for a variety of social and academic purposes. Prerequisites: INTL 2043 and INTL 3043. Online Spring 1…

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: Model U.N. Seminar
courses.description: Students study the issues and procedures of the United Nations. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor is required. Also listed as HIST 3080 and PSCI 3080. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: permission of the instructor is required.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: Model U.N. with Practicum
courses.description: Students prepare for a regional simulation of the United Nations by learning about their country’s history, government, and foreign policy. Students enroll for this only if this is their first time attending a Model U.N. simulation as a Ouachita student. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3080. Also listed as HIST 3083 and PSCI 3083. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: permission of the instructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3080.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: Model U.N. Practicum
courses.description: Students prepare for a regional simulation of the United Nations by learning about their country’s history, government, and foreign policy. This course cannot be in the same department that HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083 was taken. Prerequisite: permission of the instructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083. Also listed as HIST 3091 and PSCI 3091. Spring.
courses.prereq_text: permission of the instructor and HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083.
prereq_other: This course cannot be in the same department that HIST/INTL/PSCI 3083 was taken.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: EST Preparation
courses.description: Readings and assignments designed to help students understand and appreciate the art and culture of Europe as experienced through an extended European Study Tour during the following May Term. Open only to students accepted to the program. Completion of this non-credit course is a pre-requisite for participating in the tour and earning credit for INTL 3433 and FINA 3163. Spring.
prereq_other: Open only to students accepted to the program.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: European Practicum
courses.description: Intensive experience of art and culture through an extended European study tour. Open only to students who have been accepted to the program. Students must enroll during May Term for both INTL 3433 and FINA 3163. Prerequisite: INTL 3400 EST Preparation.
prereq_other: Open only to students who have been accepted to the program.
courses.coreq_text: Students must enroll during May Term for both INTL 3433 and FINA 3163.
courses.offered_text: Students must enroll during May Term for both INTL 3433 and FINA 3163.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: International Studies Seminar
courses.description: This course is designed for students who have completed an overseas study experience. The course will assist in a student’s reflection on his or her overseas experience. This course is required for the minor in International Studies and must be taken the semester the student returns from a semester of study abroad. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: Second Language Assessment
courses.description: This course acquaints the language teacher with purposes and types of assessments, including self- and peer-assessments, criterion-based assessments and rubrics, and various performance-based assessment tools. Prerequisites: INTL 2043 and INTL 3043. Online Spring 2 term.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: International Study Abroad
courses.description: One or two semesters of study may be taken at an approved international site. See International Study Program. Fall, Spring.
prereq_other: Participants in any Ouachita International Study Abroad Program must be Sophomores, Juniors, or Seniors with a 2.500 cumulative GPA or higher; must be in good standing with the university; and must submit an application with recommendations from at least two Ouachita faculty members.

courses.subject: INTL
courses.subject_name: Daniel and Betty Jo Grant Center for International Education
courses.title: International Study Abroad Practicum
courses.description: A course designed to complement the international study abroad experience. Fall, Spring.
prereq_other: Participants in any Ouachita International Study Abroad Program must be Sophomores, Juniors, or Seniors with a 2.500 cumulative GPA or higher; must be in good standing with the university; and must submit an application with recommendations from at least two Ouachita faculty members.

courses.subject: ISAS
courses.title: Outdoor Physical Education
courses.description: This course will focus on physical education skills including rock climbing mountaineering, backpacking, backcountry navigation, and wilderness camping. Students will be challenged both physically and mentally as they learn the various skill sets enabling them to become comfortable in the outdoors. The course will take place in the beautiful and rugged high country of the Sierra Nevada, California, and the high-altit…

courses.subject: ISAS
courses.title: Spiritual Formation and Faith Development
courses.description: This course provides a hands -on framework for spiritual growth during ISAS. It will draw heavily on the spiritual disciplines to complement the cross -cultural, service, and adventure learning students experience during the semester. Students will have ma ny opportunities to deepen their faith in a variety of individual and corporate settings.

courses.subject: ISAS
courses.title: Leadership Education
courses.description: This course will allow each student to develop a coherent personal philosophy of leadership and explore first -hand the challenges of implementing that philosophy in real situations. Critical exploration of a variety of leadership models will be integrated with practical application. Each student will be challenged to think through and develop a distinctly Christian model of leadership.

courses.subject: ISAS
courses.title: Small Group and Interpersonal Communication
courses.description: In this course, you will study small group behavior and interpersonal communication within the contexts of current theory, pr axis, and Christian community. Course content includes the study of group dynamics, small group leadership, conflict resolution, n on-violent communication, and the application of interpersonal interaction theories.

courses.subject: ISAS
courses.title: Cross-Cultural Ministry
courses.description: During this course, students will interact with people from diverse backgrounds and cultures. These interactions will help broaden their perspectives on people and cultures different from their own. Students will become more effective witnesses for the G ospel because they have successfully transferred learning about others in different cultures back to home and school. They will see firsthand that the Kingdom of God…

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Elementary Italian I
courses.description: A course in the fundamentals of grammar and composition, using the conversational approach. Readings and multimedia presentations on the elementary level stimulate interest in Italian culture. On Demand.

courses.subject: ITAL
courses.title: Elementary Italian II
courses.description: A course in the fundamentals of grammar and composition, using the conversational approach. Readings and multimedia presentations on the elementary level stimulate interest in Italian culture. On Demand.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Elementary Japanese I
courses.description: Courses in the fundamentals of Japanese. Initial instruction utilizes Romanized Japanese, but students are introduced to the writing system of Japanese. Both semesters should be taken. On Demand.

courses.subject: JAPN
courses.title: Elementary Japanese II
courses.description: Courses in the fundamentals of Japanese. Initial instruction utilizes Romanized Japanese, but students are introduced to the writing system of Japanese. Both semesters should be taken. On Demand.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Concepts of Wellness
courses.description: Students will examine their fitness needs, producing an exercise program and lifetime personal fitness goals. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Foundations of Kinesiology
courses.description: An introductory course in the disciplines of physical education, sport and leisure studies for the major/minor. Basic concepts, principles and the changing nature of this multifaceted field will be studied. Prerequisite to all required KIN courses. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Fundamental Motor Development
courses.description: A systematic study of motor and skill development from childhood through adulthood with special emphasis upon the conditions for effective motor learning. Prerequisite: KIN 1003. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Outdoor Leisure Pursuits
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce outdoor leisure activities, along with basic skills and techniques needed to continue li fe-long participation leading to the development of a healthier active lifestyle. The student will gain information about outdoor r ecreation resources in the community and learn to make full use of them. Activities which may be incorporated include hiking, geo cachi ng, orienteering, disc spo…
courses.prereq_text: Ability to participate and a demonstrated ability to swim
prereq_other: Ability to participate and a demonstrated ability to swim

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Drug Education
courses.description: An exploration of the physical, mental, emotional, and social aspects of drug use and abuse. Special attention will be focused on proper use of drugs in contemporary society. On Demand.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Health and Safety
courses.description: A course that deals with the principles of personal health, health risk and appraisal, and interpersonal relationships. Issues in nutrition, exercise, mental health and mental illness, stress, domestic violence and prevention of chronic disease. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Structural Basis of Human Movement
courses.description: A study of human movement from an anatomical perspective as it applies to physical activity. KIN majors or permission of inst ructor. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Methods of Strength Training and Conditioning
courses.description: A study of the methodology of teaching various strength and conditioning programs to prepare strength coaches, personal trainers, and health club professionals. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Care and Prevention of Injuries
courses.description: This course is designed for those seeking admission into a master’s degree program in athletic training, sports medicine, and health care professions. Using outcomes-based curriculum, proven methods of sports injury evaluation, therapy and return to play d ecisions will be addressed. Laboratory times will focus on introducing the clinical skills necessary for admission to the above -mentioned programs. Prerequisites:…

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Physiology of Exercise
courses.description: A study of bodily functions under the stress of muscular activity. Prerequisite: KIN 1003, 1113, KIN 2093 or BIOL 2014. Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Program Design and Management
courses.description: This course covers the principles of planning and implementing general leisure programs designed for group involvement. Topics include identification of leisure needs, categories of leisure activities, programming formats, and integration of people with di sabilities into general leisure programs. Upon completion, students will be able to develop and implement activities based upon participants’ needs, interests, and…

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Adapted Kinesiology Methods
courses.description: A course designed to help prepare the exercise-related professional to meet the needs of the disabled in schools and society. Prerequisites: KIN 1003, 1113, 2093. Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Methods of Physical Activity for Children
courses.description: An activity class to give prospective teachers a broad range of developmentally appropriate activities for the different deve lopmental skill levels of elementary age children with implications for physical education, program content, teaching techniques, a nd materials. Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Methods of Teaching and Coaching
courses.description: This course is designed to assist students in becoming skilled and knowledgeable in teaching and coaching individual and team activities. Emphasis will be placed on developing and evaluating the student's skills and knowledge. Fall.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Organization and Administration of Kinesiology Programs
courses.description: A study of issues facing administrators in exercise-related professions. Special emphasis is placed on programs, policies, procedures, and problems influencing leaders in the areas of health, physical education, recreation and sports. Prerequisites: KIN 1003, 1113, and 2093 for KIN Major; Junior standing for Business Administration Major with Sport Management Emphasis. [CW3] Fall.
courses.prereq_text: KIN 1003, 1113, and 2093 for KIN Major; Junior standing for Business Administration Major with Sport Management Emphasis

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Field Experience in KIN-Senior BA (Non-Teaching Emphasis) Candidates Only
courses.description: This class represents the culmination experience of our undergraduate degree program. It will be used as a “steppingstone” for employment for students. It is viewed as an “apprenticeship” as students will be placed under a mentor in the field outside the university setting. Field experiences are generally 10 weeks in length. Classroom experience will be prior to and after the field experience. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Exercise Prescription and Testing
courses.description: A study of the guidelines for exercise prescription, programming, and testing for generally healthy persons as advised by the American College of Sports Medicine and the National Strength and Conditioning Association. Prerequisites: KIN 3023. Fall.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Biomechanical Analysis
courses.description: A study of body movements, of muscle and joint action in relation to physical activity. Mechanical analysis of the more commo nly used physical skills is studied. Prerequisite: KIN 1003, 1113, KIN 2093 or BIOL 2014. Fall.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Methods and Materials in Health, PE, and Wellness Education
courses.description: The theory and methods utilized in effective health, physical education, and wellness instruction. Prerequisite: KIN 1003. Fall.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Personal Trainer
courses.description: This advanced elective course is designed to prepare students to integrate strength and conditioning knowledge and skills obt ained in specific coursework and to apply this in preparation for the National Council on Strength and Fitness (NCSF) Personal Trai ning certification exam. Students completing this course will have the opportunity to sit for the NCSF exam. Prerequisites: KIN 1003, 1113, 2093, and 4043. On Dem…

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: This seminar encourages students to integrate knowledge and skills from their major field of study with the broader liberal arts experience provided by the Ouachita Core Curriculum. The course provides a basis for life-long learning, meaningful work, and service to humans in a diverse and interconnected world. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Health Promotion Seminar
courses.description: This course will focus on community health needs in specific demographic areas of need. Students will be engaged in improving health literacy for select populations. On Demand.

courses.subject: KIN
courses.title: Special Studies
courses.description: A course designed to provide an opportunity to do advanced research or independent work in an area of special interest. On Demand.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Elementary Latin I
courses.description: An introduction to classical Latin. The course focuses on grammar, syntax, and vocabulary. On Demand.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Elementary Latin II
courses.description: A continuation of LATN 2203. On Demand.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Intermediate Latin I
courses.description: A course focusing on the upper reaches of classical Latin grammar and syntax. On Demand.

courses.subject: LATN
courses.title: Intermediate Latin II
courses.description: A course focusing on the translation of various classical Latin poems and prose pieces. On Demand.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: College Algebra
courses.description: A study of the properties and applications of linear, exponential, logarithmic, quadratic, and polynomial functions, as well as an introduction to absolute value, piecewise, and rational functions. Additional topics will include transformation and composit ion of functions, as well as matrices and their use in the solution of linear systems. Prerequisite: An MPI of 75 or higher. Fall, Spring.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: College Algebra with Review
courses.description: A version of MATH 1003 with additional contact hours in order to provide just-in-time review and extra support. Prerequisite: An MPI of 65 or higher, or a grade of C or better in ASKL 1023. Fall, Spring.
courses.prereq_text: An MPI of 65 or higher, or a grade of C or better in ASKL 1023
prereq_other: An MPI of 65 or higher, or a grade of C or better in ASKL 1023

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Mathematics for the Liberal Arts
courses.description: Students will engage in a study of mathematical ideas and thinking, learning to solve problems and make decisions using sound quantitative reasoning. All students will study techniques of problem-solving, mathematical reasoning, the set of real numbers, sizes of infinity, and the use of analogy to explore four-dimensional geometry. Additional topics will be chosen by the instructor and may include the use of mathemat…

prereq_other: An MPI of 65 or higher, or a grade of C or better in ASKL 1023

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Precalculus
courses.description: A course designed to prepare students for Calculus. Topics include functions, polynomials, rational functions, exponential an d logarithmic functions, circular functions, systems of linear equations and coordinate geometry. Prerequisite: An MPI of 80 or higher, or a grade of C or better in MATH 1003 or MATH 1004. Fall.
courses.prereq_text: An MPI of 80 or higher, or a grade of C or better in MATH 1003 or MATH 1004
prereq_other: An MPI of 80 or higher, or a grade of C or better in MATH 1003 or MATH 1004

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Introduction to Cryptology
courses.description: This course explores the science of communication security. Students explore a variety of historical approaches to encryption , the cryptanalysis techniques that arose to crack those codes, and some of the more modern mathematical algorithms commonly used i n practice today. Mathematical content includes counting, probability, elementary number theory, modular arithmetic, matrices, and primality testing. Prerequisite…
